situation:
You chaired a call with Nadia Novak, a planning peer in Sweden, after on-time-in-full delivery to one customer of a diabetes product dropped to 82 percent and the account manager complained. You now need to send the follow-up email. Your notes:
- OTIF 82 percent in September, target is 95
- Root cause: two inbound lots of pen needles arrived late
- Nadia to confirm revised customer allocation by Friday
- You to share a recovery plan with weekly OTIF figures by 4 November
- Open point: who briefs the account manager
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Nadia for the call and state that you are writing about the drop in OTIF.
Summarise the root cause and the decision taken, quoting the 82 percent result and the 95 percent target.
List each action with its owner and date, then ask who will brief the account manager.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Quality found the same particulate in three consecutive batches of an oncology infusion packed in Germany, and the investigation points to a stopper component from Peter Larsen's company. You need his team to explain what happened and confirm which component lots are affected before the next packing slot on 18 November. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the same particulate appeared in three consecutive batches and was traced to your stopper component.
Request a written root-cause report and the list of affected component lots by 8 November.
Ask Peter to confirm containment measures so the packing slot on 18 November can go ahead.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, thank you for the invitation to the S&OP review on Tuesday 12 November at 10:00. We have booked our cold-chain team for it and prepared the capacity view for the biologic. Can you confirm the time is fixed? We also need your updated volumes by Friday so we can reserve the refrigerated trucks for Brazil. Best regards, Oliver" The review has to move because your regional lead is travelling that week, so write back to Oliver and apologise for the inconvenience.
tasks: Apologise for the change and explain that the review moves because the regional lead is travelling.
Answer Oliver's question about whether the time is fixed by proposing a new date and hour.
React to his Friday deadline for volumes and say when you will send them.

situation: A batch of a vial-based injectable has been on hold since Monday because the executed batch record from the Singapore site is missing signatures on two pages, and a deviation investigation is open. Release is planned for 20 November and a customer shipment depends on it. Ben Ahmed leads documentation in the other region and has not answered your earlier chaser. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the batch has been on hold since Monday because of the missing signatures in the batch record.
Explain the impact on the shipment of 6,000 vials and the customer date of 20 November.
Ask Ben to send the corrected pages by Thursday and to name one contact for the investigation.

situation:
You attended a workshop with Priya, a planning peer, about a pilot of automatic safety-stock recalculation for an active ingredient. It will run in Mexico and Colombia first, and you must now send a follow-up email. Your notes:
- Pilot starts 3 December in two countries
- Recalculation runs monthly; planners may override by up to 10 percent
- Priya documents the override rules by 15 November
- You choose the accuracy metric and share it by Friday
- Review after eight weeks, go or no-go in February
Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Thank Priya for the workshop and summarise the pilot scope and its start date.
List the actions with owner and deadline so nobody has to reread the notes.
Ask Priya to confirm the override rule before you share the plan with the wider team.

situation:
You joined a call with Amira Tanaka, a colleague in the Japan region, about a paediatric suspension whose delivery arrived on time but cannot be released because the certificate of analysis is missing. You must now write the follow-up. Your notes:
- 12 pallets arrived on 14 October
- Certificate of analysis still missing, release blocked
- Supplier promises it by Wednesday noon
- Amira asks Japan quality whether a provisional review is possible
- You move 3 pallets to Monday's truck
- Osaka customer warned of a possible two-day delay
- Open point: should a second testing lab be qualified
Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Summarise the problem: an on-time delivery that cannot be released without the certificate of analysis.
List the six agreed steps with owners and the Wednesday and Monday dates.
Flag the open question about qualifying a second testing lab and ask for Amira's view.

situation: Your monthly S&OP review with a UK supplier of a secondary packaging component is booked for Tuesday 12 November, but your regional lead will be travelling that week and cannot attend. You want to move it with as little disruption as possible and still hear the supplier's capacity view. Write to Amira, your main contact there, and stay friendly.
tasks: Explain that the monthly review has to move because your regional lead will be travelling.
Offer two alternative time slots in the following week and ask which one suits Amira's team.
Ask her to send the capacity comments before the new date so the meeting stays short.

situation: A valve supplier in Chile delivered components for an inhaler nine days late. The delay will not hurt this month's output, because you re-sequenced the lines, but it uses up all the safety stock planned for next month. Andre, your contact at the supplier, should know what this means for his schedule. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Tell Andre that the late valve delivery will not reduce this month's inhaler output.
Explain that it consumes all the safety stock planned for next month, leaving no buffer.
State the next step: you need a firm delivery date and a weekly status from him.

situation: Stability samples of an inhaler must reach a laboratory in Mexico by Friday, but standard freight will arrive on Monday and the test window would be lost. An express courier costs about 1,800 dollars and Amira, who controls the regional budget, must approve it. Write to her and make clear why this cannot wait. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that the stability samples must reach the laboratory by Friday and standard freight would arrive too late.
Request approval for the 1,800 dollar express courier cost to be charged to the regional budget.
Ask for her answer by Wednesday noon so the pick-up can be booked.

situation:
You attended a formal review with your manager, Elena Hall, about the demand baseline of an oncology infusion in Canada, where the stockpiling seen during the pandemic years has disappeared. You must now send a written summary. Your notes:
- Stockpiling pattern from 2021 gone; orders 18 percent below old baseline
- Statistical model still trained on 2021 and 2022 data
- Decision: exclude those two years and retrain
- New baseline of 1,150 units a month from January
- You rerun the forecast by 8 November
- Finance receives the lower revenue view by 15 November
- Open point: keep a 5 percent buffer for tender volumes?
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise why the baseline needs a reset, quoting the 18 percent gap against the old level.
Record the decision and the new figure of 1,150 units a month, with the dates for each action.
Ask Elena to decide on the 5 percent tender buffer, which remains unresolved.

situation: From next month, every region will write its demand-review notes on one standard template, and your region in Singapore is among the first to adopt it for a paediatric suspension. You are informing Fatima Kowalski, a planner in another team, because her notes will have to follow the same layout. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Announce that all regions will use one standard template for demand-review notes from next month.
Describe the three sections: assumptions, risks and actions, each limited to one page.
Say that Fatima should send her feedback by 15 November, before the first use in December.

situation: A supplier business review for a device sub-assembly is booked on 20 November, which is also the first day of the internal audit. You own the data for both and cannot cover them, yet nobody consulted you before the invitation went out. Write to your manager, Amira Hall, and ask her to sort it out. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Point out that the supplier business review on 20 November falls on the first day of the audit.
Explain why you cannot cover both, since you prepare the sub-assembly data for each.
Ask Amira to approve a one-week postponement and to inform the supplier.

situation: Your manager Carlos keeps asking for the Canadian forecast of a paediatric suspension to match last year's volumes, but the stockpiling that inflated them is gone and orders are about 15 percent lower. You have asked twice for the target to be reset and nothing has changed. Write to him and make the case clearly. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the pandemic-era stockpiling has disappeared and last year's volumes no longer reflect real demand.
Show the evidence: orders about 15 percent lower for four months in a row.
Ask Carlos to approve a reset of the baseline and the target before the December forecast cycle.

situation:
You chaired a call with Katarina Ahmed, a packaging vendor for an inhaler in Chile, who wants to change from weekly to fortnightly deliveries. You must now send a friendly follow-up. Your notes:
- Proposal: deliveries every two weeks from February
- Vendor offers a 9 percent price reduction in return
- Our concern: carton cover falls to 6 days
- Agreed to test with at least 10 days of cover
- Katarina sends the revised price table by 22 November
- You model stock cover on both lines by 29 November
- Open point: penalty if a delivery slips by more than two days
Keep the tone friendly.
tasks: Thank Katarina for the open conversation and summarise her proposal and your cover concern.
Confirm what was agreed, including the test with ten days of cover, and the two deadlines.
Raise the unresolved penalty question and suggest discussing it on the next call.

situation: You negotiated a penalty-free window of ten working days for forecast revisions with a vendor of clinical-supply kits. Elena, a peer in Australia, sent her revision on day eleven and the vendor now talks about a fee. This is the second time her team missed the window, and you want it to stop. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Remind Elena that the agreed penalty-free window for forecast revisions lasts ten working days.
Explain that her latest revision arrived on day eleven and may trigger a fee.
Ask her to send future revisions by day eight and confirm that her team can do that.

situation: You are arranging a two-day visit to a supplier's inhaler site, planned for 12 and 13 December. You want your manager, Oliver Petrov, to know the plan before it is booked: two nights in a hotel near the site, a first-day plant tour, and a second-day session on capacity and lead times. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Oliver that you plan to visit the supplier's site on 12 and 13 December.
Outline the agenda: a plant tour on the first day and a capacity session on the second.
Say that you will send the full itinerary and cost estimate once the supplier confirms the dates.

situation: A standard template for demand-review notes is being introduced across regions, and Amira Reyes in Ireland runs the respiratory product review that you attend remotely. You would like her team to use the template for the next meeting and send you the notes the same week. You know her workload is high, so stay friendly.
tasks: Introduce the new standard template for demand-review notes and say why regions are adopting it.
Ask Amira to use it for the next respiratory review and send the notes by Friday.
Offer a short call to walk through the template and invite her comments.

situation: A delivery for an oncology infusion in Ireland arrived on time, but the certificate of analysis from the manufacturer is late, so the lot cannot be released yet. The wholesaler needs it next Tuesday. You expect the certificate within two days and want your manager, Peter, to stay calm. Keep the tone reassuring.
tasks: Tell Peter that the delivery arrived on time but cannot be released without the certificate of analysis.
Reassure him by saying the certificate is expected within two days and the Tuesday date is still safe.
Explain the next step: you will chase the manufacturer daily and report back on Thursday.

situation: An intern joins your planning team for three months starting on 4 November, and she will study cold-chain flows for a biologic. Oliver works in the Turkey region and knows the local cold-chain distribution better than anyone. You want an hour of his time each week. Write to him in a friendly way.
tasks: Introduce the intern and explain that she joins the planning team for three months from 4 November.
Ask Oliver for one hour each week to explain cold-chain distribution in Turkey.
Offer to share her project outline and ask when he is free for a first call.

situation: Your manager, Julia Ruiz, told the packaging vendor of an inhaler that you could accept deliveries every two weeks, without checking with planning first. Cover for cartons would drop to about six days, which leaves almost no room for a delay, and the Turkish plant is already tight. Write to her to raise the matter. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that you learned the vendor was told fortnightly deliveries are acceptable, before planning could review the risk.
Explain that carton cover would fall to about six days and leave no buffer.
Ask Julia to hold the answer to the vendor until planning has presented a stock-cover analysis.

situation: A raw-material specification for a prefilled pen was changed by the supplier without any notice to you, and you only found out when the incoming inspection in Japan flagged a different particle size. The lot is blocked and the change should have gone through a formal notification. Nadia Novak is your account contact. Sound disappointed but professional.
tasks: Explain that the incoming inspection found a changed particle size that you were never told about.
State that the specification change should have been notified under your quality agreement.
Ask Nadia for the change documentation and a plan so this cannot happen again.

situation:
You attended a meeting with Lucas, a peer in Chile, about a business case for a data-quality clean-up of the master data behind a paediatric suspension. The project would take about three months. You now send a follow-up email. Your notes:
- Master data errors cause about 4 percent of forecast bias
- Project of three months, two analysts half-time
- Cost estimate 38,000 dollars
- Lucas drafts the business case by 20 November
- You supply five examples of wrong lead times by Friday
- Decision at the planning council on 4 December
Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Summarise the problem and the proposed three-month clean-up, quoting the 4 percent bias.
List the actions with owner and date, including the council meeting on 4 December.
Ask Lucas to confirm the 38,000 dollar estimate before it goes into the business case.

situation: Your forecast for an oncology infusion in Brazil will change in the next planning cycle, and you want to avoid a fee for a late revision. Kenji Kowalski, a supplier contact, is open to a flexible arrangement. You would like a penalty-free window of ten working days after each forecast release. Write to him in a friendly way.
tasks: Explain that your forecast may change again and that you want to avoid fees on late revisions.
Propose a penalty-free window of ten working days after each forecast release.
Ask Kenji to reply by next Friday and offer a call to agree the exact wording.

situation: An intern started with your planning team last Monday and still has no access to the planning system, because the access request sits with Fatima Moreau's regional team in Australia. The intern has been shadowing for five days with nothing to do. You have already sent a reminder. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the intern started last Monday and still has no access to the planning system.
Explain that without access the intern cannot work on the inhaler project and has been idle for five days.
Ask Fatima to grant the access by Wednesday or tell you what is blocking it.

situation:
You joined a call with your peer Elena Petrov in Italy about an expedited courier needed for a critical shipment of a paediatric suspension. You must now write the follow-up. Your notes:
- Sample shipment must reach the lab by 14 November
- Express courier costs 2,100 euros
- Elena approves the cost this week
- You book the pick-up for Monday
- Open point: which cost centre is charged
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise the reason for the express courier and the 14 November deadline.
Record the agreed actions, naming who approves the cost and who books the pick-up.
Ask Elena to confirm the cost centre, since this is still undecided.

situation:
A project you led has ended and day-to-day support for an inhaler planning tool goes to the operations team in Japan. You met your peer Chloe Ruiz to agree the handover and now send the follow-up. Your notes:
- Project closes on 30 November
- Operations take support from 1 December
- You deliver the user guide and a list of known issues by 22 November
- Chloe's team trains two people in the first week
- You stay available for questions until the end of January
Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Chloe for the productive meeting and confirm the handover date of 1 December.
List what each side delivers, including the user guide and the training in the first week.
Say how long you remain available for questions and invite her to flag gaps early.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, the Brazil team says the 50 mg kit could run out in about three weeks, and the next shipment lands only on 2 December. Do we have any option to bring something forward? Also, who should I tell at the hospital network if we cannot? Thanks, Andre" Reply to Andre in a friendly way and tell him what you can do and what you cannot.
tasks: Answer his question about options by saying what stock can be moved forward and from where.
React to the date of 2 December by explaining the realistic earliest arrival.
Tell Andre whom to inform at the hospital network and what to say.

situation:
You attended a formal meeting with your manager, Marta Silva, after a logistics provider announced a 6 percent rate increase for oncology infusion shipments to Chile. You must now write up the follow-up. Your notes:
- Increase of 6 percent from 1 January
- Annual impact about 90,000 dollars
- Counter-offer: 3 percent with a volume commitment
- You prepare the volume forecast by 14 November
- Marta calls the provider's account lead on 18 November
- Fallback: request quotes from two other providers
- Open point: who signs the volume commitment
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise the provider's increase and its annual cost, quoting both the percentage and the amount.
Describe the counter-offer and the fallback, with owners and dates for each step.
Ask Marta to decide who signs a volume commitment, since that remains open.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, the customer in Cairo says their invoice shows 12,000 packs of the tablet, but they counted only 11,400 on receipt. They want a credit note by Friday. Can you check the delivery documents and tell me what to say? Kind regards, Andre Walsh" Reply formally, saying what you will check and when.
tasks: Acknowledge the invoice mismatch of 600 packs and confirm you are checking the delivery documents.
Say when you will report back, with reference to the customer's Friday request.
Advise Andre what to tell the customer in the meantime about the credit note.

situation:
You attended a call with your manager, Viktor, because a shipment of a cardiovascular tablet got stuck at customs in India late in the evening and must be handed to a team in another time zone. You now send a friendly follow-up. Your notes:
- Shipment held since 22:00 India time, missing import licence
- Handover to the Indian team at 08:00 their time
- You send the licence copy and customs contact tonight
- Viktor informs the customer about the delay
- You check progress at 14:00 tomorrow
Keep it friendly.
tasks: Confirm that the shipment is stuck for a missing import licence and the issue is being handed over.
List the actions with owners and times, including your licence copy and the customer message.
Say when you will check progress and invite Viktor to raise anything you missed.

situation: A pallet of secondary packaging components is stuck late at night, and you will be offline until the morning. Priya Hall works in the Egypt region, where the team is awake and covers the same supplier. You want her to take over the issue tonight. Write to her in a friendly way.
tasks: Explain that a pallet of packaging components is stuck and you will be offline until the morning.
Ask Priya to take over the issue and name the supplier contact she should call first.
Say where you saved the shipping documents and promise a full update when you are back.

situation: A customer's warehouse in Poland rejected a shipment of clinical-supply kits last Thursday because the packing list was missing the batch numbers. Ingrid Reyes, a peer, prepares the shipping documents for that lane and should have checked them. The study start is now delayed by three days. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the warehouse in Poland rejected the shipment because the packing list lacked batch numbers.
Describe the consequence: a three-day delay to the study start and extra freight costs.
Ask Ingrid to add a document check before dispatch and confirm by Friday that it is in place.

situation: You have been coordinating with a customer's warehouse in South Africa to pick up a pallet of a vial-based injectable. The warehouse offered a window on Thursday between 08:00 and 11:00, and the transporter has accepted it. You want Nadia Novak, who covers that customer in the other region, to know the plan. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Nadia that the pallet pick-up is set for Thursday between 08:00 and 11:00.
Explain that the warehouse and the transporter have both accepted this window.
Say you will send the pick-up confirmation on Wednesday and ask her to warn the customer.

situation: From January, every planning report in your area must follow a new naming convention that starts with the region code, then the product and the month, for example PL_VIAL_2025-01. Reports with older names will be rejected by the shared folder. You are telling Lucas, a peer in Poland, who owns several monthly reports. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Inform Lucas that a new naming convention for planning reports becomes mandatory from January.
Give the pattern and one example so he can rename his monthly reports.
Explain that old names will be rejected and ask him to finish renaming by 15 December.

situation: A deviation at a supplier's site in India for a cardiovascular tablet was closed two weeks late, and the batch release date of 22 November is now at risk. The final investigation report is still missing. Yuki Costa is your quality contact there. Ask for what you need quickly, and be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that the deviation closed two weeks late and puts the 22 November release date at risk.
Request the final investigation report within 48 hours.
Ask Yuki to confirm who can approve the batch record the same day it arrives.

situation: For the third month in a row, tablets from your German packing line show tiny fibres, and the cause has been traced to the blister foil from Yuki Kowalski's company. Rejected packs are costing you roughly 2,000 euros a month and delaying shipments. You want a lasting fix, not another apology. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the same fibres have appeared for three months and trace to the blister foil.
Quantify the cost of rejected packs, about 2,000 euros a month, and the shipment delays.
Ask Yuki for a corrective action plan with dates by the end of next week.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, forecast accuracy for the inhaler dropped to 71 percent last month, well under the 85 percent target. Planning needs to explain this at Thursday's review. Can you tell me what happened and why it was not flagged earlier? Thanks, Carlos Reyes" One large unexpected order caused the miss, and the sales team in Ireland never told you about it. Reply firmly but politely.
tasks: Explain that a single large order, unknown to planning, caused the drop from 85 to 71 percent.
Answer his question about why it was not flagged earlier by describing when you first saw it.
Propose that sales alert planning about orders above a set size before Thursday's review.

situation: You start parental leave on 1 December. Your open purchase orders for a respiratory product are going to Sofia, who will cover for you. Your manager, Rahul, wants to know the handover is under control. You prepared a list of 14 open orders with their delivery dates and supplier contacts. Keep it friendly.
tasks: Tell Rahul that Sofia will cover your open purchase orders from 1 December.
Describe what you prepared: a list of 14 open orders with dates and supplier contacts.
Say when the handover meeting happens and how Sofia can reach you in an emergency.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, we took over the biologic shipment last night, but the handover note had no temperature logger data and the reefer showed 9 degrees at 03:00. Who decides whether we release the truck? I need the logger file today. Regards, Peter" Reply firmly but politely, since the data was in your handover.
tasks: Point out that the logger file was attached to the handover email and say where to find it.
Answer his question: state clearly who makes the release decision and by what time.
Propose a standard handover checklist so both regions share the same information in future.

situation:
You attended a meeting with Samir Ahmed, a peer in Mexico, about the end-of-month inventory reconciliation, which will now have a stricter cut-off. You must now send the follow-up. Your notes:
- New cut-off: working day 3 at 12:00
- Late adjustments are posted into the next month
- Samir updates the checklist by 8 November
- You brief your team on Monday
- First use for the November close
- Open point: exceptions for oncology infusion lots
Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Samir and summarise the new cut-off time for the monthly inventory reconciliation.
List the actions with owner and date, ending with the first use in the November close.
Ask Samir how oncology infusion lots should be treated, since that is still undecided.

situation: You are a demand planner for an inhaler portfolio, and your request for 4,200 euros of training budget has just been approved. The money will cover a supply chain planning certification for two people on your team. Hannah Costa, a peer who runs the planning team in Brazil, shares your cost centre and needs to know how this affects her. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Hannah that the training budget has been approved and name the two colleagues who will attend the certification.
State the total amount, the March start date, and how the cost will be split between cost centres.
Ask her to confirm by Friday that the arrangement is acceptable and explain the next administrative step.

situation: Laura Nair, a colleague in the Japan planning office, sent the invitation for Thursday's monthly review of the prefilled pen supply plan. It went to an outdated distribution list, so your regional logistics lead and two forecasters never received it, and the review cannot start without them. You want the invitation corrected and a workable time agreed. Keep the tone neutral and factual.
tasks: Explain that the invitation reached an outdated distribution list and name the three people who are missing from the meeting.
Describe why the review cannot be useful on Thursday without the logistics lead and the forecasters present.
Request that she resend the invitation to the correct list and propose two alternative time slots.

situation: You are a supply planner for clinical-supply kits. Hannah, a peer in finance planning in the UK, has held your request for a three-week safety-stock buffer worth about 380,000 pounds for two weeks without a decision. The first trial site opens on 12 November, and the buffer must be ordered before then. Raise the delay with her and ask for an answer this week. Stay neutral and factual.
tasks: Open by referring to your request from two weeks ago and say that it is still without a decision.
Explain the risk to the trial start on 12 November if the buffer is not ordered by Friday.
Ask Hannah to approve the amount or list the exact information she still needs from you.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I have good news: Emre, a new planner from our Turkey office, will join your team for a week of shadowing from 3 November. Could you let me know which meetings he should sit in on, and whether you can lend him a desk? I would also like him to see how you build the monthly forecast. I need your answer by Wednesday. Thanks, Chloe" Reply to Chloe with a clear plan for his week.
tasks: Confirm that Emre is welcome and say which two planning meetings he should attend during the week.
Answer her question about the desk and suggest a day when you can show him the monthly forecast build.
Ask whether he needs system access before 3 November and promise to send a daily schedule on Wednesday.

situation: A tender customer in Canada has asked for written assurance of supply on a clinical-supply kit for the next twelve months. Your manager, Kenji Moreau, told the sales team this could be signed, but the current plan covers only seven months because of limited filling capacity. You are worried about a promise the plan cannot support. Raise this with Kenji before anything is sent. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that sales has been told the supply assurance can be signed, while the plan covers only seven months.
Explain which capacity limit prevents you from supporting twelve months and what it would take to remove it.
Ask Kenji to hold the letter until you have reviewed it together and to suggest a time on Tuesday.

situation: You have been working with Laura Lindqvist, a peer who leads planning in South Africa, on a proposal to share one regional analyst between your two departments. The analyst's yearly cost is about 62,000 euros, and you suggest a 60/40 split starting in January. Your finance contact has not yet seen the proposal. Update Laura on where it stands. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Tell Laura that you have drafted the cost-sharing proposal and summarise the 60/40 split starting in January.
Describe what the analyst would work on for each department and how his time would be tracked.
Say you will send the draft to finance on Monday and ask her to comment before then.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, our demand review wants to raise the January to March forecast for the cardiovascular tablet by 25 percent, because two hospital tenders may be extended. We would like you to confirm that supply will follow. Could you do that before our review meeting on Friday? Best regards, Peter Tanaka" Planning does not fully trust a manual override without evidence. Reply to Peter accordingly.
tasks: Thank Peter for the update and say that you cannot yet confirm a full 25 percent increase.
Ask for evidence of the tender extensions, such as dates and expected volumes, before Friday's review meeting.
Offer to commit supply for a smaller increase now and agree when you will revisit the rest.

situation:
You chaired a short review with your manager, Tom Brandt, after a vial-based injectable nearly ran out in South Africa. The reorder point had been set on old demand and the system raised no alert. You must now send him a follow-up email. These are your notes:
- Reorder point based on 2023 demand, now 30% too low
- No system alert because stock never crossed the old threshold
- Emergency order of 8,000 vials placed Monday, arrives 14 Nov
- Anna to recalculate all reorder points by 8 Nov
- Open point: who approves the cost of the emergency freight?
tasks: Summarise what went wrong with the reorder point and why the system gave no alert.
List each action with its owner and date, including the emergency order and Anna's recalculation by 8 November.
Flag the freight approval as the open point and ask Tom to confirm who decides.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, we heard that you will start a weekly exception-based planning routine next month. Does this mean you will stop sending us the full forecast every Monday? Our production team needs it to book capacity, and we are worried about missing a change. Please explain what we should expect and what you need from us. Kind regards, Peter Silva" Explain the new routine to Peter in your reply. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Confirm that the weekly exception-based routine starts next month and explain what it means for the Monday forecast.
Tell Peter what you expect from his team, such as flagging capacity limits by Thursday each week.
State that the process will not be postponed and offer a short call to answer his remaining questions.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, a new colleague, Aiko, joins our Japan team on Monday and she will need access to your weekly inventory and OTIF reports. Could you add her to the distribution today? It would save us time. Many thanks, Rahul" The reports contain customer data, so access must go through a formal approval. Reply to Rahul and explain what he must do. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say that you cannot add Aiko to the distribution today because the reports contain restricted customer data.
Explain the approval step: Rahul's manager must request access through the data owner, which takes about two days.
Offer a summary version of the OTIF report that you can send her on Monday.

situation: A colleague from commercial finance, Marina, is moving into supply planning for a cold-chain biologic next month. Lucas Haddad, a peer in Brazil, trained two new planners last year and has a good onboarding pack. You would like to borrow it and have him join her first week. Write to him in a friendly way, since you do not work together every day.
tasks: Introduce Marina, explain that she is moving from commercial finance, and say when she starts in supply planning.
Ask Lucas to share the onboarding pack he used last year, especially the glossary and the lead-time overview.
Suggest a thirty-minute video call next week with Marina and offer to return the favour.

situation: From next month, the day-to-day relationship with the packaging supplier for an inhaler will move from planning to procurement. Until now you handled orders, delivery questions and the monthly review. Your manager, Sofia Moreau, in Italy, asked to be kept informed. Write her an update on how the handover will work and what she can expect. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Sofia that supplier responsibilities move to procurement from the first of next month and name the new contact.
Explain which tasks procurement takes over and which two planning tasks stay with you.
Describe the handover meeting you have planned and ask Sofia whether she wants to join it.

situation:
You attended a call with your manager, Rahul Reyes, about a cold-chain data logger that failed during a shipment of a paediatric suspension to Germany. You must now send him a formal follow-up. These are your notes:
- Logger stopped recording after 14 hours in transit
- Shipment of 12 pallets held at the German warehouse
- Quality to decide on release by Thursday
- Carrier to supply backup temperature data by Wednesday
- Replacement shipment of 4 pallets prepared as a contingency
- Open point: who pays if the lot is rejected?
tasks: Summarise the deviation and the decision to keep the twelve pallets on hold until quality reviews them.
List the actions with owners and deadlines, including the carrier's backup data and the contingency shipment.
Raise the cost question as the open point and ask Rahul to confirm who will decide.

situation: Peak season for an active ingredient starts in six weeks, and your team is already at its limit. You want to hire a temporary planner for three months, which needs about 18,000 euros of extra budget. Oliver Ahmed, a peer in Germany, owns the shared planning budget and can support the request. Ask him in a friendly way to back it.
tasks: Explain that peak season starts in six weeks and your team cannot cover the extra workload.
State the cost of a three-month temporary planner and ask Oliver to support the request from the shared budget.
Suggest a short call this week and say what information you can send beforehand.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, as you know I am moving to the demand team in two weeks, so I am looking for someone to take over the safety-stock review for secondary packaging. My notes are spread over a shared drive, two spreadsheets and some old emails. Could you take it over? I can walk you through it on Tuesday or Thursday. Thanks, Priya" Reply to Priya in a friendly way.
tasks: Accept the safety-stock review in principle and thank Priya for offering a walk-through.
Choose Tuesday or Thursday for the session and ask her to gather the notes in one folder beforehand.
Ask which items in the review are still unfinished and when the next review meeting takes place.

situation: The qualification of a new sub-supplier for a secondary packaging component is moving more slowly than promised. The supplier's audit report is late, and the delivery date for the first lot shifts by three weeks, from 18 November to 9 December. Andre Nair, a colleague in the German planning office, is waiting for these components. Update him on the delay and what you will do. Keep it neutral.
tasks: Inform Andre that the first lot will now arrive on 9 December instead of 18 November.
Explain that the delay comes from the late audit report and say what the supplier has promised.
Describe the next step you will take, such as checking current stock, and say when you will update him again.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I heard that the excipient lot for the cardiovascular tablet is late. How late is it, and does it affect our deliveries in Sweden? I have a meeting with the commercial team this afternoon and I would like to know what to say. Rahul" The supplier had a raw-material shortage, and the lot is nine days late. Reply to Rahul.
tasks: Confirm that the excipient lot is nine days late and explain that the supplier had a raw-material shortage.
Say whether Swedish deliveries are affected, using the current stock and the expected production date.
Suggest what Rahul can tell the commercial team this afternoon and promise a new update on Friday.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, our stock of the active ingredient will run out in about ten days. Could your site send 400 kg by air freight this week? I know it is costly, but sea freight takes five weeks. Please tell me soon. Elena" You saw her first message three days ago and have not replied. Reply to Elena and be apologetic.
tasks: Apologise for answering three days late and acknowledge that her stock will run out in ten days.
Explain that the air-freight cost of about 400 kg still needs approval, and say who will decide and when.
Offer a partial shipment of 150 kg by air now and the remainder by sea.

situation: A colleague from another country, Daniel Tanaka, will visit your site in Chile for a planning workshop. He changed his travel dates twice without telling you, and the invitation letter for his visa was issued for the first dates only. You are concerned that he may not get a visa in time. Write to him and ask him to fix the situation. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Say that the invitation letter was issued for the original dates and no longer matches his travel plans.
Explain that the visa office needs the final travel dates by Monday to process the new letter.
Ask Daniel to confirm his dates in writing and tell him what you will do once you have them.

situation: A batch failure at the manufacturing plant means your clinical-supply kit will have only two weeks of cover in the next quarter. Laura, a peer in Australia, holds some spare kits that her studies will not need before March. You would like to borrow them and replace them when the next batch arrives. Write to her in a friendly way.
tasks: Explain that a batch failure leaves the next quarter with only two weeks of cover.
Ask Laura whether she can lend you part of her spare kits, naming roughly how many you need.
Promise to replace the kits from the next batch and suggest a quick call tomorrow.

situation: Responsibility for a prefilled pen supplier was moved from planning to procurement six weeks ago. However, the supplier still sends delivery questions and invoices to you. Ingrid Ahmed, the procurement lead in the Italy office, has not yet confirmed who contacts the supplier. You want this settled so that nothing is missed. Write to her to raise the problem. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that responsibility for the supplier moved to procurement six weeks ago, yet queries still reach you.
Give one example of a message that the supplier sent to you last week and the risk of missing it.
Request that Ingrid confirm the new contact person by Friday and inform the supplier in writing.

situation: A critical sample shipment of prefilled pens must reach the laboratory in Chile by Thursday, and standard freight would take a week. You requested approval for an expedited courier at 1,150 dollars, and your manager has just agreed. Tom Rossi, a colleague in the Chile office, is waiting for the samples. Update him on the plan. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Tom that the expedited courier has been approved and the samples should arrive by Thursday.
Share the tracking arrangement and the pickup time so that he can prepare the laboratory to receive them.
Ask him to confirm receipt and to flag any customs problem immediately.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, thanks for your proposal for a temporary planner for the oncology peak season. I can probably find 10,000 euros, but you asked for 16,000. Can you manage with fewer weeks? And can you tell me what happens if we do not hire anyone? Laura" Reply to your manager Laura Larsen in a friendly way.
tasks: Thank Laura for the partial funding and say whether ten weeks instead of fourteen would work.
Describe the risk of leaving the peak without extra support, such as late orders and more overtime.
Suggest a plan for the gap in budget and ask for a decision by next Monday.

situation: A customer in Brazil received the wrong pack size of a paediatric suspension, a 100 ml bottle instead of 250 ml, and asked for an immediate replacement. You have arranged a replacement shipment for Thursday and the wrong bottles will be collected. Nadia Brandt, who works with the Brazil customer team, needs the details. Update her in a friendly way.
tasks: Tell Nadia that the replacement 250 ml bottles will ship on Thursday and give the expected delivery date.
Explain how the incorrect 100 ml bottles will be collected and who at the customer should prepare them.
Apologise for the mix-up on behalf of the team and say that you will check the cause.

situation: A packaging vendor for a paediatric suspension wants to change the delivery frequency from weekly to every two weeks. Your manager, Julia Kowalski, in Japan, is worried about stock and costs. After a call with the vendor, you believe the change is manageable if you increase the order size slightly. Update her and help her feel at ease.
tasks: Explain that the vendor wants biweekly deliveries and that you have already checked stock cover for Japan.
Reassure Julia that a slightly larger order of 5,000 units avoids any risk of a stock-out.
Say what you will agree with the vendor next and when you will report back.

situation: A transport vendor in Turkey has proposed to send the service-level report every quarter instead of every month. For a respiratory product with tight delivery windows, you want the monthly cycle. Lucas Walsh, a peer who owns the transport contract, can raise this in the next contract meeting. Ask him for his support. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that the vendor proposes a quarterly service-level report and that you want to keep it monthly.
Give one concrete reason, such as late deliveries that a quarterly report would reveal too slowly.
Ask Lucas to raise the point at the contract meeting and tell you the outcome.

situation:
You joined a call with a supplier, Kenji Rossi, who offered a 9 percent discount on an oral solid dose tablet but with a minimum order quantity that is three times higher. You must now send a friendly follow-up to him. These are your notes:
- Discount of 9% on the current price
- MOQ rises from 50,000 to 150,000 packs
- Shelf life of 36 months limits how much you can hold
- You will model the total cost by 12 Nov
- Kenji to check a 100,000-pack option
- Open point: payment terms after the first order
tasks: Thank Kenji for the call and summarise the discount offer together with the higher minimum order quantity.
List the actions: your cost model by 12 November and his check of the 100,000-pack option.
Mention the open question about payment terms and ask him to reply by next Friday.

situation: Last week you had to pay for an air-freight transfer of a device sub-assembly so that the Italy line could keep running. The shortage came from a forecast that Mark, a peer in the supplying site, shared late and with a large error. The extra cost was about 14,000 euros. You are disappointed. Write to Mark, stay professional, and ask for a solution.
tasks: Describe the air-freight transfer and how the late forecast with a large error led to it.
State the extra cost of about 14,000 euros and explain how this affects your budget.
Ask Mark to agree on a deadline for future forecast updates and suggest a meeting to review the process.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the carrier told me that no temperature-controlled truck is free on Thursday, the day we agreed for the respiratory product pick-up in Sweden. Do we wait until Monday or look for another carrier? Please tell me what you recommend. Oliver" Reply to your manager with a clear recommendation.
tasks: Recommend one option, waiting until Monday or switching carrier, and give your main reason briefly.
Explain the impact on the customer's delivery date and the stock available if you wait.
Say what you will do next, such as contacting two other carriers by noon.

situation: A customer's warehouse in Australia rejected a shipment of a cardiovascular tablet because the documentation was incomplete: the certificate of analysis was missing. The pallets are now waiting at the port. Yuki Rossi, a colleague in the regional quality office, can issue the document. Write to Yuki and ask for it, keeping the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that the customer's warehouse rejected the shipment because the certificate of analysis was missing.
Request the corrected document by tomorrow noon and state the batch number it must cover.
Mention that the pallets are waiting at the port and ask Yuki to confirm when you can expect the file.

situation: A batch failure at the Turkey plant leaves a respiratory product with only two weeks of cover next quarter. You learned about it from a colleague, not from the site, and the plant did not warn you when the first tests failed. Laura Moreau, a colleague in the Turkey site planning team, is responsible for sharing such news. Write to her. Be disappointed but professional.
tasks: State that you learned about the batch failure from a third party and not directly from the site.
Explain the consequence: only two weeks of cover next quarter and a risk of backorders.
Ask Laura to confirm the recovery plan and to alert you on the same day when future tests fail.

situation: Over the last month, a supplier in Ireland has sent a respiratory product in partial shipments, usually two or three per order. This makes goods receipt untidy and complicates your planning, because you cannot tell when an order is complete. Peter Larsen, a peer in the Ireland warehouse team, handles receipts. Give him a friendly update on what you plan to change.
tasks: Say that partial shipments have become frequent and describe how they affect the order status in your system.
Explain what you will change, such as asking the supplier to confirm full quantities before dispatch.
Ask Peter to note the delivery note numbers on each partial receipt and send you a weekly list.

situation: A retained sample of an oral solid dose tablet from your supplier in Mexico showed an out-of-specification result for dissolution. The lot is on hold, and your plan depends on its release in two weeks. Fatima Reyes, a quality contact at the supplier, must organise a retest. Write to her to raise the problem and keep the tone formal.
tasks: Identify the lot number and report the out-of-specification dissolution result found in the retained sample.
Request a retest under documented conditions and ask for the preliminary result within five working days.
Explain the impact on your supply plan if the lot is not released in two weeks.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, from 1 December we will track purchase order confirmations in a new tool instead of the shared spreadsheet. Could you confirm that your team will use it and nominate one person for the training on 20 November? I need an answer by Friday. Best regards, Priya" Reply to Priya formally.
tasks: Confirm that your team will use the new tool from 1 December and thank Priya for the notice.
Nominate one colleague for the training on 20 November and give the reason for your choice.
Ask whether the old spreadsheet history will be migrated and who owns the data.

situation: A shipment of an oncology infusion arrived from India with labels showing the expiry date as 03/11/2027, which your warehouse reads in two different ways. The shelf life is critical, and the lot cannot be released until it is clear. Peter Reyes, a contact at the supplier, can confirm the date. Ask him for help in a friendly way.
tasks: Explain that the expiry date on the labels can be read as 3 November or 11 March.
Ask Peter to confirm the correct date in writing and to send a copy of the batch record.
Request that future labels use a clear format with the month written as letters.

situation: Seasonal demand for a respiratory device is starting about three weeks earlier than your model predicted, and orders from a distributor in Poland have already increased by 20 percent. To plan production you need the customer's own view. Andre Petrov is the purchasing contact there. Ask him for an updated order forecast. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Say that demand is rising earlier than expected and that your orders from Poland are up about 20 percent.
Ask Andre for an updated order forecast by week for the next ten weeks.
Explain why you need it by Friday and what you will do after receiving it.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I read your idea of sharing a regional analyst between our departments, and I like it. Two questions: who would be the analyst's line manager, and how would we split the cost of the oncology reports? Could you also tell me when you want to start? Katarina" Reply to Katarina in a friendly way.
tasks: Thank Katarina for her interest and answer who would be the analyst's line manager.
Propose a cost split for the oncology reports and explain the reasoning behind your numbers.
State a start date and suggest the next step, such as a short call with both finance teams.

situation: Because of a reorganisation, a half-finished forecast analysis for a respiratory product was handed to you by Andre, a peer in Ireland. The file has no notes, three versions of the model and no explanation of which assumptions were used. You have a review next week. Write to Andre to raise the problem and ask for what you need. Stay neutral.
tasks: Explain that the handover file has three model versions and no notes on the assumptions used.
Ask Andre which version is current and to describe the main assumptions for the winter months.
Request a thirty-minute call before your review next Tuesday.

situation: You and Andre Walsh, a peer in Australia, agreed to share a regional analyst for a paediatric suspension, with Andre's team using about 30 percent of the analyst's time. In October, his team used nearly half, but the invoice still shows the 30 percent split. Write to him formally to raise the discrepancy and ask for a correction.
tasks: Refer to the agreed 30 percent share and note that October usage was closer to 50 percent.
Ask Andre to review the time log you attach and either adjust the split or explain the difference.
Propose a monthly check of the hours to avoid further disagreement.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, I understand you want an expedited courier for the oncology infusion samples at about 2,300 Canadian dollars. Before I sign, please tell me why standard shipping is not enough, what the deadline is, and whether the cost can be shared. Regards, Marta Lindqvist" Reply to Marta formally.
tasks: Explain why standard shipping is not enough, giving the delivery time against the laboratory deadline.
State the exact deadline and the consequence of a late delivery for the study.
Answer her question about sharing the cost and request her approval by midday tomorrow.

situation:
You joined a call with Elena Tanaka, who coordinates a customer's warehouse in Singapore, to agree the pick-up of a pallet of device sub-assemblies. You must now send her a friendly follow-up email. These are your notes:
- Pick-up window Tuesday 10:00 to 12:00
- Six pallets, total weight about 1,800 kg
- Driver must bring the booking reference
- Elena to reserve loading dock 3
- You send the packing list by Monday
- Open point: who takes the empty pallets back?
tasks: Thank Elena for the call and confirm the pick-up window and the number of pallets.
List who does what and by when, including the loading dock and the packing list on Monday.
Raise the question about the empty pallets and ask her to reply before the weekend.

situation:
You and your peer Marta Novak met a transport vendor that delivers a secondary packaging component to Poland. The vendor wants to report service levels only every quarter, while you want monthly reports. These are your notes from the call.
- Vendor proposal: service-level report once per quarter
- Our position: monthly, with on-time-in-full and damage rate
- Compromise: monthly for six months, then review together
- Marta checks the penalty clause with legal by 14 March
- You send the report template by Friday
- Vendor shares January and February data by 20 March
- Open point: who pays for the extra data extraction
tasks: Open with a warm thank-you to Marta and summarise the compromise reached on the report cycle.
List the actions with their owners and dates, including the template, legal check and vendor data.
Flag the open point about extraction costs and ask Marta how she wants to handle it.

situation: You work in supply planning at a pharmaceutical company. Pharmacy orders for a paediatric suspension in Spain started rising in the second week of October, about five weeks before the seasonal model predicted. Tom, who owns the regional demand inputs in another region, did not warn you, and you had to expedite two shipments. You want the early signals shared in future. Write in a neutral tone.
tasks: Explain that respiratory demand in Spain began earlier than the seasonal model assumed, citing the order data.
Describe the impact: two expedited shipments and lower cover on the suspension this month.
Ask Tom to share early pharmacy signals every week and to agree a point of contact.

situation:
You attended a short call with Chloe Ruiz and her team in another region about a vial-based injectable for Japan. The consignee moved to a new warehouse, but several open orders still carry the old shipping address. Your notes are below.
- New warehouse address effective 3 November
- Seven open orders still show the old address
- Chloe's team updates the customer master data by Wednesday
- You review the open orders and reissue the documents
- Any shipment already in transit gets a redirect request
- Check again on Friday that no order points to the old site
tasks: Thank Chloe for the quick call and say why you are writing to confirm what was agreed.
Summarise the address change and list who does what by which date.
Ask Chloe to confirm the plan and say you will check the orders on Friday.

situation: You are a supply planner in Italy. The contract for a secondary packaging component expires in January, and you asked your colleague Priya Walsh in procurement to include a clause covering partial deliveries. The draft she sent yesterday does not mention it, and last quarter a full order was held back for two weeks because of a small shortfall. You feel let down. Sound disappointed but professional.
tasks: Say you reviewed the draft renewal and noticed that the partial-delivery clause you requested is missing.
Remind Priya of last quarter's delay and what it cost your planning in the packing lines.
Propose a concrete wording, such as shipping at least 80 percent on time, and request a revised draft.

situation:
You joined a call with Elena Hall, a distributor customer in South Africa, to discuss why the statistical forecast and the commercial forecast for a cardiovascular tablet differ so much for the next two months. These are your notes.
- Statistical forecast: 120,000 packs per month
- Commercial forecast: 190,000 packs per month
- Gap comes from a planned tender, not yet confirmed
- Elena confirms tender result by 12 December
- Until then plan on 150,000 packs per month
- You review stock cover at the distributor on Monday
- Open point: who bears the cost of excess stock
tasks: Summarise the two forecast figures and the working assumption of 150,000 packs agreed until the tender result.
List the actions with owners and dates, including Elena's tender confirmation and your stock review.
Ask Elena to confirm the notes and raise the unresolved question about excess stock costs.

situation: You are a planner preparing a business case for a data-quality clean-up project of about three months to fix item master data for a cardiovascular tablet. Ingrid Novak in the Mexico finance team has not answered your submission since two weeks ago, and the budget window closes on Friday. You need her feedback soon. Keep a disappointed but professional tone.
tasks: Mention that you submitted the business case two weeks ago and have received no feedback yet.
Explain the cost of delay: wrong lead times in the system keep creating avoidable shortages.
Ask Ingrid for a decision or specific questions before Friday, and offer a short call.

situation: You coordinate outbound shipments of a device sub-assembly. A pallet must be collected from your customer's warehouse in Germany next week, and the site only accepts trucks in narrow slots. Katarina, who works in the logistics team in that region, knows the dock schedule. You want to agree a window. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Greet Katarina and explain that a pallet needs collecting from the customer's warehouse next week.
Propose two possible pick-up windows and mention any limit, such as the driver's waiting time.
Ask her to confirm one window and send the dock contact details by Thursday.

situation: A shipment of a respiratory product was due in Poland this Friday, but the receiving dock will be closed for inventory that day. Peter, who manages inbound planning in the Polish team, can accept it on Monday morning. You must ask him to confirm the new date. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State that the Friday delivery cannot be received because the dock is closed.
Request that the delivery moves to Monday morning and ask whether a specific time slot is available.
Ask Peter to confirm in writing so you can update the carrier and the customer.

situation:
You had a handover meeting with your manager Viktor Brandt because the owner of the weekly prefilled-pen supply report in Italy is leaving at the end of the month and you will take it over. Your notes are below.
- You own the report from 1 December
- Current owner trains you on two Tuesdays
- Report goes out every Monday by 9 a.m.
- Two data sources are manual and should be automated
- Viktor approves a review of the format in January
tasks: Thank Viktor and confirm that you will take ownership of the weekly report from 1 December.
Summarise the training plan, the Monday deadline and the manual data sources you want to automate.
Ask Viktor to confirm the timing of the January review and who attends.

situation: You manage a warehouse in Chile that holds an oncology infusion for a supplier. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, this is Peter from the supplier. Four of our colleagues will visit your warehouse on Thursday 13 November. Could you tell us what safety briefing they need and which route they should follow inside the building? We also need to know if the cold room is part of the visit. Thanks and best regards, Peter" Reply to Peter and answer each point. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Confirm the visit on Thursday 13 November and describe the safety briefing every visitor completes on arrival.
Explain the route through the building and answer whether the cold room is part of the tour.
Ask Peter to send the visitors' names and say who will meet them at reception.

situation: You plan supply of a prefilled pen for Japan. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, we have won a hospital tender, and we expect demand for the prefilled pen to rise by 25 percent next quarter. Can you confirm that you will supply the full extra volume from 1 January? Please reply by Friday. Kind regards, Julia Reyes" Answer her request. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Thank Julia for the early notice and say you can commit to part of the extra volume now.
Explain what is needed for the rest: the written tender confirmation and an updated forecast by a given date.
Give a clear deadline for her reply and say when you will confirm the full supply plan.

situation: A hospital customer in India has told you that its remaining stock of an oncology infusion will last only ten days. Your colleague Ben is the account contact. You have already asked for an expedited shipment that should arrive in six days. You want to calm the situation. Keep a reassuring tone.
tasks: Explain that you understand the hospital has ten days of stock left and take it seriously.
Describe the expedited shipment, its expected arrival in six days and the buffer it gives.
Say what you will check daily and promise an update tomorrow afternoon.

situation: You work in planning in Egypt. Last week a delegation visited your warehouse, and nobody had planned the safety briefing or the walking route, so the visit started with a delay of forty minutes. Your manager Oliver arranged it with two days' notice. A visit of this kind is coming again next month. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain that last week's visit began forty minutes late because no safety briefing or route was prepared.
Describe the risk to staff safety and to the oral-dose stock if visitors move without a plan.
Request that Oliver assign an owner and give at least one week's notice for the next visit.

situation: A prefilled-pen shipment to a customer in Chile was rejected at the warehouse door. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I have just heard that the customer refused the delivery because the documentation was incomplete. Can you tell me what was missing and when the pallet will be accepted? The customer is already asking questions. Thanks, Chloe Ahmed" Reply to your manager and apologise. Keep an apologetic tone.
tasks: Apologise for the rejected delivery and explain that the batch certificate was missing from the paperwork.
Describe how you are fixing it today and give the new expected acceptance date.
Say what check you will add so incomplete documentation is caught before dispatch.

situation: A customer in Spain has sent an invoice for an oral solid dose tablet that shows 12,000 packs, but only 10,800 packs were delivered according to the receipt. Your manager Mark must approve a credit note before it can be issued. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the invoice and the delivery receipt differ by 1,200 packs and give the order number.
Request Mark's approval to issue a credit note for the difference.
Ask for a decision by Wednesday so the customer receives the correction before month end.

situation: An intern will join the planning team for three months, and the message below arrived this morning. "Hello, our intern Lukas starts on Monday and I would like him to work in your team for the first month. Please give him full access to the planning system and assign him a mentor from day one. Many thanks, Katarina Hall" You can help, but full access in week one is not possible. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Welcome the idea of hosting Lukas and confirm that you will be his mentor.
Explain why full system access is not possible in week one and offer read-only access first.
Propose a week-by-week plan and ask Katarina to confirm the manager approval for access.

situation: Your team is introducing a new naming convention for planning reports, mandatory from January. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, I heard that file names for our weekly capacity reports will change next year. Could you send me the new format, and will the old names still be accepted in December? Best wishes, Mei" Answer her two questions. Use a neutral tone.
tasks: Confirm that the new naming convention applies to all weekly capacity reports from January.
Give the exact format with one example file name and state that old names work until 31 December.
Offer a short call and ask Mei to send a test file by mid-December.

situation: A recurring particulate finding in a cold-chain biologic has been traced to one packaging component. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, the investigation shows that the particles come from the stopper lot. Please quarantine all stock from that lot and tell me how many units are affected by Wednesday. Regards, Hannah Nair" You agree, but you need the hold to be scoped carefully. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Confirm that you will quarantine the affected stopper lot and send the unit count by Wednesday.
Ask Hannah to confirm in writing which lot numbers are included, so unaffected stock is not blocked.
Explain the supply risk of a wider hold and ask for a release decision date.

situation: A key account in Sweden has demanded a recovery plan after a stock-out of a cardiovascular tablet. Your manager has asked you to write it by Thursday, but you have no input from commercial or manufacturing, and they have not answered your requests. You feel unsupported. Sound disappointed but professional.
tasks: Say you are working on the recovery plan for the Swedish key account and the Thursday deadline.
Explain that commercial and manufacturing have not provided the volumes and dates you need.
Ask Elena to push both teams for their input by Wednesday noon, otherwise the plan will be incomplete.

situation:
You held a formal review with Daniel Hall at a supplier in Germany after a change control for an oral solid dose tablet was put into use before final quality approval. These are your notes.
- Change implemented on 6 October, approval signed on 20 October
- Fourteen days of production affected
- Supplier opens a deviation by Monday
- Daniel provides impact assessment by 7 November
- Affected batches stay on hold until review
- Supplier updates its procedure before next change
tasks: Summarise the facts of the unapproved change and the batches that remain on hold.
List the agreed actions with owners and dates, including the deviation and impact assessment.
Ask Daniel to confirm the content and flag the procedure update as an open point to track.

situation: A supplier has offered a 12 percent discount on a secondary packaging component but wants the minimum order quantity raised from 20,000 to 80,000 units. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I think the discount looks great, so I would accept the offer. What do you think? Can you send your view before the call on Thursday? Elena" You disagree because of storage and expiry of artwork. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Thank Elena and say that you do not support accepting the offer as it stands.
Explain the storage space, artwork-change risk and cash tied up by an order four times larger.
Suggest a counter-proposal, such as a smaller increase, and agree what to say on Thursday's call.

situation: You are helping organise a team offsite, and the message below arrived this morning. "Hi, we have 6,000 euros for eight people for two nights in Valencia. Could you propose a hotel and room setup, shared if needed, and tell me the total cost? I would like to decide on Friday. Thanks, Andre Okafor" Reply with a proposal. Use a neutral tone.
tasks: Propose one hotel option and a room layout, such as four twin rooms, that fits the budget.
State the total cost for two nights and the amount left under 6,000 euros.
Mention one alternative and ask Andre to choose by Friday so you can book.

situation: A quality deviation for a packaging component was closed late, which puts a release date at risk. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Sir or Madam, our deviation report was closed four days late, so the certificate will be issued on 21 November instead of 17 November. We understand this affects your plan. Please tell us if this is acceptable. Kind regards, Mark Ruiz" Reply in a formal tone.
tasks: Acknowledge the delay and say that the new certificate date of 21 November is not acceptable.
Explain the consequence for your release date and downstream shipments if the certificate arrives later than 18 November.
Request an expedited review and a written confirmation of the earliest date.

situation: A batch of an oncology infusion failed quality tests, so only two weeks of cover remain for next quarter in Singapore. Your customer contact Peter Nair needs a clear picture, not an alarm. You have asked manufacturing for a replacement slot but there is no confirmed date. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Inform Peter that a failed batch leaves only two weeks of cover for next quarter.
State what is known and unknown: the replacement slot is requested but not yet confirmed.
Explain how you will allocate current stock and promise a status update every Friday.

situation:
You chaired a meeting with Daniel Reyes and the shipping team in Canada about moving open shipment issues for a vial-based injectable from email chains to a shared tracker. Your notes are below.
- Tracker replaces email for all open shipment issues from 1 December
- Every issue gets one owner and a due date
- Daily five-minute review at 10 a.m.
- You build the template this week
- Daniel trains the Canadian team by 28 November
tasks: Summarise the decision to use a shared tracker instead of email chains from 1 December.
List who does what and by when, including your template and Daniel's training session.
Ask the team to confirm they can attend the daily review and to suggest changes before Friday.

situation: Your logistics provider has announced a 6 percent rate increase on active-ingredient shipments from India starting in January. Your manager Ben is worried about the budget. You have not accepted the increase and plan to counter with a volume-based offer. Keep a reassuring tone.
tasks: Tell Ben about the 6 percent increase and say that you have not accepted it.
Describe your counter-offer, such as a smaller increase in return for a guaranteed annual volume.
Explain the next steps and when you expect the provider's answer, with a fallback estimate for the budget.

situation:
You met your manager Oliver to discuss a supplier delay. Only half of the glass vials ordered for a respiratory product in Brazil arrived, and the supplier gave no date for the rest. These are your notes.
- Delivered: 150,000 vials of 300,000 ordered
- No date yet for the remaining 150,000
- Current vial stock covers three weeks
- Supplier to give date by Thursday
- Plan B: ask second supplier for 50,000 vials
- You reduce the batch size of the next run
- Escalate to the supplier's director if no date by Friday
tasks: Summarise the shortfall and the three weeks of vial cover left.
List the actions with owners, including the supplier date, the second supplier request and the smaller batch.
Ask Oliver to confirm that you can escalate to the director on Friday if needed.

situation: A change in the pack size of an oral solid dose tablet was loaded into the planning system before final quality approval. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, I noticed that planning already uses the new pack size, but quality approval is not complete. This may cause problems at audit. Can you explain what happened and how you will correct it? Nadia Novak" Reply and apologise. Sound apologetic.
tasks: Apologise for loading the new pack size before quality approval and explain how it happened.
State what you did to correct it: reverse the data and block orders for the new size.
Describe the safeguard you will add and ask Nadia to confirm the date of final approval.

situation: A colleague from the commercial function is moving into supply planning for an inhaler in Australia next Monday. Your manager Priya Rossi asked you to prepare her arrival. You have set up system access, booked two training sessions and chosen a buddy. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Priya that the new colleague starts on Monday and that system access is already prepared.
Describe the two training sessions you booked and the buddy you assigned for the first month.
State what you still need from her, such as approval of the training budget, before Friday.

situation: A graduate rotating through your team in Turkey for six months needs a first project. You think a good one is cleaning up the lead-time data for an oral solid dose tablet, which is small, useful and safe for a beginner. Your manager Marta must agree. Use a neutral tone.
tasks: Tell Marta that the graduate needs a first project and that you have one in mind.
Describe the lead-time data clean-up, its expected duration of six weeks and the benefit to the team.
Ask Marta to approve the project and tell her you will introduce the scope on Monday.

situation:
You met your manager Mei Ahmed to ask for approval to extend the licence of your forecasting tool for one more year. The tool is used for a vial-based injectable in South Africa. Your notes are below.
- Licence expires 31 January
- Cost for one more year: 24,000 euros
- Tool gives forecast accuracy gain of 6 points
- Mei approves extension in principle
- Finance needs the purchase request by 5 December
- You send a usage summary to Mei by Friday
- Alternative tool to be reviewed next year
tasks: Summarise the decision to extend the licence and the cost and accuracy gain behind it.
List actions with owners and dates, including your usage summary and the purchase request.
Ask Mei to confirm the approval formally and mention the review of alternatives next year.

situation: A new joiner on the demand planning team in South Africa needs read-only access to your weekly oncology infusion reports. You are not allowed to share them without the approval of the report owner, your colleague Amira. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Introduce the new joiner and state why access to the weekly reports is needed.
Request read-only access to the report folder and name the data she needs to see.
Ask Amira for her decision by Friday and say that the manager can confirm the business need.

situation: A respiratory product has just received regulatory approval in Ireland, and you expect a demand spike that no history in your system can explain. Your peer Amira Novak launched a similar product in another country last year. You want to borrow her approach. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Congratulate Amira on her recent launch and explain that you face a similar one in Ireland.
Request her launch curve or the assumptions she used, and ask what she would change.
Suggest a thirty-minute call this week and offer to share your results afterwards.

situation: Three weeks ago you submitted a business case for a data-quality clean-up project of about three months for an inhaler. Fatima Fischer, who leads planning in Singapore, is waiting for news. The regional budget committee meets on Wednesday and has put your case on the agenda. Use a neutral tone.
tasks: Update Fatima that the business case is on Wednesday's budget committee agenda.
Summarise the cost, duration and expected benefit in two sentences.
Explain what happens after the decision and when you will send the result.

situation:
You held a formal call with your peer Katarina Rossi about giving a new joiner in another region access to your reports on a cold-chain biologic in Germany. The notes are below.
- New joiner starts 1 December in the Rome office
- Access limited to three reports
- Katarina signs the access request by Friday
- You create the folder and permissions by 28 November
- Data privacy training required first
- Review access after 90 days
- Open point: whether she needs the cost data
tasks: Summarise what was agreed about the joiner's start date and the three reports she can view.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the access request and the privacy training.
Ask Katarina to confirm the notes and flag the open question about cost data.

situation: Last week you asked the Australian team for access for a new joiner who needs your inhaler reports. Tom Silva in that region has now set it up, and you have a few details to pass on: which reports she can open, who her contact is and when the training starts. Keep a neutral tone.
tasks: Inform Tom that the access was set up and list the reports the new joiner can open.
Name her contact person on your side and explain how she should ask for help.
State the training date and ask Tom to tell you if any report fails to load.

situation: A senior director at a customer has asked for a call with your management after repeated delays of an active ingredient. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, after the third late delivery, our director would like to speak to your management next week. Could you arrange it? Fatima" You agree and want to show you take it seriously. Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Fatima for the message and say that you understand why the director wants a call.
Offer two time slots next week and name the manager who will join.
Describe briefly the improvements you will present, such as a firm delivery plan for the next three shipments.
