situation: Your supplier of a cardiovascular tablet in Australia has told you that its capacity is reduced after a planned maintenance shutdown ran two weeks over. Your manager Tom Kowalski must know what this means for the next two months. Your tone must be formal.
tasks: Report that the supplier's maintenance shutdown ran two weeks over and that capacity is now reduced.
Quantify the expected shortfall and the packs at risk over the next two months.
Describe the mitigation you propose and request Tom's decision on it by Thursday.

situation: Your team is moving open shipment issues from email chains to a shared tracker. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I like the tracker idea but I worry about double work. Do we still email the carrier? And who closes an issue once it is solved? Peter Ahmed" Answer his two questions and keep the tone friendly.
tasks: Thank Peter for the feedback and acknowledge his concern about double work.
Answer both questions: say whether emails to the carrier continue and who has the right to close an issue.
Invite him to the ten-minute walkthrough on Wednesday and ask for further suggestions.

situation: A shipment of a diabetes product got stuck in customs at 11 p.m. in Mexico, and you could not reach anyone in the team that covers the next time zone. The handover instructions were unclear. Your manager Ingrid Hall has asked for feedback. You are disappointed but want to stay constructive.
tasks: Describe what happened with the customs issue and the time you spent finding the right person.
Explain which parts of the handover were unclear, such as contact numbers and who has authority at night.
Propose a one-page handover checklist and ask Ingrid to approve it this month.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the supplier business review for the clinical-supply kit is set for Thursday, but our internal audit has just booked the same morning and I cannot be released. Could we push the review back by a week? I know the supplier already has the agenda. Please tell me today so I can update the invitation. Regards, Lucas Fischer" Lucas works in the Poland office. Reply to him: you can accept the delay, but you need the supplier's scorecard data first. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Thank Lucas for the warning and say you can accept moving the review to the following Thursday.
Insist that the supplier scorecard data reaches you by Monday, so the review is not delayed twice.
Offer to contact the supplier yourself today and ask Lucas to send the updated invitation.

situation: From next month, open shipment issues for a paediatric suspension will be logged in a shared tracker instead of long email chains. Chloe leads distribution in India and her team still answers by email. You want her to agree to try the tracker for the next four weeks and nominate one person to keep it updated. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Explain briefly why the shared tracker replaces the email chains for open shipment issues.
Ask Chloe to name one person in India who will update the tracker every day.
Propose a four-week trial and offer a short walkthrough call this week.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, good news and bad news. Sweden will launch the cardiovascular tablet six weeks earlier than planned, now on 3 March. That means the first stock must reach our warehouse by mid-February. Can you tell me whether supply can cover the extra volume, and what you need from me? Thanks, Yuki" Yuki is a colleague in another region. Reply with a friendly answer that deals with her questions.
tasks: Thank Yuki for the early notice and confirm that you understood the new 3 March launch date.
Say whether supply can reach the warehouse by mid-February, and name one risk.
List what you need from Yuki, such as the revised forecast, and give a deadline.

situation: Last Tuesday a shipment of device sub-assemblies reached your site in Canada with labels showing the expiry date as day-month-year instead of the agreed year-month-day format. Two pallets were held back by quality. Andre Silva manages dispatch in another region, and this is the second case this year. You must report the deviation, request a correction, and ask for a written corrective plan. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State which shipment arrived with wrong expiry date labels and how many pallets quality held back.
Explain the effect on your site, mentioning that this is the second similar case this year.
Request a written corrective action plan and a relabelling decision by the end of next week.

situation: During the pandemic your customer in Poland ordered far more oral solid dose tablets than normal, and your forecast still contains that stockpiling pattern. Orders have since returned to a lower level. Kenji Silva at the customer planning team must confirm the real expected volumes so you can reset the baseline before Friday's planning run. Be polite but make the urgency clear.
tasks: Explain that the old stockpiling pattern is gone and your forecast baseline needs a reset.
Ask Kenji to send his expected monthly volumes for the next two quarters.
Stress that you need his answer before Friday's planning run and thank him in advance.

situation: Your latest projection shows that stock of a prefilled pen in Sweden will go negative in about six weeks unless something changes. The customer's planner, Andre, has not yet shared the confirmed orders for the next quarter. You need those orders and a decision about an earlier delivery slot. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Warn Andre that projected inventory of the prefilled pen turns negative in about six weeks.
Request the confirmed orders for next quarter by the end of this week.
Ask whether he can accept an earlier delivery slot, and propose a call to agree it.

situation:
You chaired a short meeting with your manager about a contractor who will cover a maternity leave in the respiratory product team in India. Your notes are below. Write the follow-up email to Chloe Larsen.
- start date 4 Nov, contractor Ben
- week 1: ERP and planning tool training, owner Alex
- week 2: shadow the weekly supply review
- access to shared drive pending, IT, by 1 Nov
- review progress on 15 Nov, Chloe to approve extension
tasks: Summarise the agreed ramp-up plan, including Ben's start date and the training in week one.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the IT access request due 1 November.
Ask Chloe to confirm the plan and the progress review on 15 November.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I checked the numbers again. A rounding error in the planning tool understated the demand for the respiratory product by about four percent per month over the three-month horizon. This may explain why we are short in Japan. I will send you the corrected file later. Can you hold the next shipment until then? Thanks, Chloe" Reply as a firm but polite peer.
tasks: Thank Chloe for finding the rounding error and acknowledge the four percent monthly gap.
Explain that you cannot hold the next shipment, because the current Japan stock is already tight.
Ask her to send the corrected file by tomorrow and offer to rerun the plan together.

situation: Your company just won a tender in Egypt, and demand for an oncology infusion next quarter will rise by 25 percent. Priya, who runs planning in another region, is worried because her sites share the same supply. You want to inform her of the change, explain how you will protect her allocation, and say what happens next. Sound reassuring.
tasks: Announce the tender win and the expected 25 percent rise in next quarter's demand.
Reassure Priya that her allocation stays protected and say how you will check this.
Describe the next step, such as a supply review on Monday, and invite her questions.

situation: Daylight saving time ends in a few weeks, and the weekly planning sync for the clinical-supply kit will land at an awkward hour for the team in Turkey. Rahul Ruiz coordinates that team. You must tell him the sync moves one hour earlier from the new date and explain that nothing else about the process changes. Keep it reassuring.
tasks: Tell Rahul that the weekly planning sync moves one hour earlier after daylight saving ends.
Give the exact new time in both time zones and the first date of the change.
Say the agenda stays the same and ask him to tell you if the new slot is a problem.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I saw the supplier is only at 70 percent capacity after the maintenance shutdown ran two weeks long. Why did we not hear this earlier? The Singapore clinical-supply kit orders for November now look at risk. Please explain and tell me your plan. Daniel" Daniel is your manager. Reply with an apologetic tone and a clear plan.
tasks: Apologise to Daniel for not escalating the capacity problem as soon as the shutdown overran.
Explain the current 70 percent capacity and what it means for the November kit orders.
Present your plan, such as prioritising orders, and promise an update on Friday.

situation: The temperature-controlled truck booked to collect device sub-assemblies on Wednesday is no longer available because the carrier lost a vehicle. The new pick-up could be Friday morning. Mark Ahmed manages receiving in Ireland, and his team has already scheduled staff. Tell him about the change and what you are doing to limit the delay. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Mark that the temperature-controlled truck is unavailable on Wednesday and give the reason.
Propose Friday morning as the new pick-up and delivery date and explain the delay.
Describe the steps you are taking, and say when you will confirm the final slot.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, we have about 12,000 pounds of unused budget for clinical-supply kit transport this quarter. Could we move it to next quarter instead of losing it? I need to know by Thursday whether you agree, because finance closes then. Thanks a lot, Sofia" Sofia works in the UK office. Answer in a friendly way.
tasks: Thank Sofia and say whether you agree to move the 12,000 pounds to next quarter.
Mention one condition, such as listing the planned transport costs the money will cover.
Confirm that you will answer finance before Thursday and ask her to send the details.

situation: A shipment of an oncology infusion is waiting at the border in Australia because a customs document is missing. The delay is already costing a day of storage. Samir Reyes at the supplier prepared the paperwork and should be able to issue the missing certificate quickly. Ask him for the document and a short confirmation of when it will arrive.
tasks: Explain that the oncology infusion shipment is held at the Australian border because one customs document is missing.
Ask Samir to send the missing certificate today and name the document clearly.
Request a confirmation of the time it will be sent and mention the storage cost.

situation: A data logger shows that a pallet of your diabetes product reached Japan after spending over two hours above the allowed temperature range. The pallet belongs to a lane handled by Priya Costa, a peer in logistics. You are unhappy because the same lane had a warning last month. You want her to investigate and tell you the root cause. Stay disappointed but professional.
tasks: Report the temperature excursion on the pallet and say how long it stayed above the range.
Remind Priya that the same lane had a warning last month and explain your concern.
Ask for a root cause investigation and a written answer within five working days.

situation: The temperature-controlled truck for your delivery of prefilled pens to South Africa cannot come on the agreed Tuesday. Daniel, your contact at the customer, expects the pens that day for a clinic programme. You need to ask him whether he can accept delivery on Thursday or help you find another carrier. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that the temperature-controlled truck cannot collect the prefilled pens on Tuesday as agreed.
Ask Daniel if he can accept delivery on Thursday, or if he knows another carrier.
Request his answer by tomorrow noon and apologise for the inconvenience.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, the prefilled pen shipment has been waiting at the Chilean border for three days. The customs office says the commercial invoice is missing a signature. Our team asked you twice. Please can you tell me what is happening? Mei" Mei works in the Chile region. Write an apologetic reply that also solves the problem.
tasks: Apologise to Mei for the three-day delay and for missing her two earlier requests.
Explain what went wrong with the commercial invoice signature and who will sign it today.
Give the expected release time and promise to update her as soon as customs confirms.

situation: A new analyst joined your team in Egypt two weeks ago and must learn the main planning systems before the month-end close at the end of the month. Your manager, Yuki Hall, asked how it is going. Give a neutral progress update: what has been covered, what is still missing, and what support you plan next.
tasks: Report what the new analyst has already learned in the first two weeks.
Point out which systems are still missing before the month-end close.
Describe next week's training plan and ask Yuki for one hour of her time.

situation: A regulatory approval in a new market has created a demand spike for an active ingredient in India, and no history can explain it. Marta, a peer in the planning team, uses your forecast for her capacity plan. You must warn her that the numbers are uncertain, explain how you built the interim estimate, and say when it will be reviewed. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Tell Marta about the approval in the new market and the unexplained jump in demand.
Explain how you built the interim estimate without historical data.
State the review date and ask her to flag capacity concerns before then.

situation: Your project for a cardiovascular tablet in Poland ends this month, and the run-state support will pass to the operations team. You are concerned because the handover plan has no named owner for deviations and the first support date is unclear. Your manager, Elena Tanaka, agreed to the plan. Raise the concern and ask for a fix. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the project ends this month and the run-state support passes to operations.
Point out that no named owner exists for deviations and the first support date is unclear.
Ask Elena to assign an owner and fix the date before the handover meeting.

situation: You would like to visit a supplier's site in Egypt for two days next month to review the tablet packing line. Amira Costa is a peer who knows the site and has contacts there. Ask her to help with the dates, the local contact and the transport from the airport. Keep it neutral.
tasks: Explain that you want to spend two days at the supplier's site next month.
Ask Amira which dates suit the site and who the local contact is.
Request advice on airport transport and thank her for any help.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, the batch of oral tablets arrived on time at our Germany site, but the certificate of analysis is still missing, so quality cannot release it. The supplier promises it by Friday. Can you push them, and can your team accept a smaller order next week? Kind regards, Hannah Rossi" Reply to Hannah in a formal style.
tasks: Thank Hannah and confirm that you will contact the supplier today about the certificate of analysis.
Respond to her question about a smaller order next week and give your decision.
Ask her to inform you immediately when the batch is released on Friday.

situation: Your manager introduced a shared tracker for open shipment issues for the diabetes product in Canada, but the old email chains still run in parallel. You now spend about an hour a day copying information. Lucas, your manager, set up the tool. Explain the problem without blaming anybody. Remain disappointed but professional.
tasks: Describe the duplicate work caused by running the tracker and email chains together.
Say that you lose about an hour a day copying shipment information between them.
Propose a clear cut-off date for emails and ask Lucas for his decision this week.

situation:
You and Samir met after an unplanned export order consumed the safety stock of a secondary packaging component in Germany. Your notes are below. Write Samir a follow-up email.
- export order of 40,000 units not in forecast
- safety stock now at 3 days
- Samir to ask supplier for an expedite by Wed
- Alex to rebuild forecast with new orders by Thu
- weekly stock check until end of month
tasks: Summarise what happened with the export order and the current safety stock level.
List the actions with owners and deadlines, including the supplier expedite and the new forecast.
Ask Samir to confirm the plan and suggest how to share future export orders earlier.

situation: Your team in Turkey is planning a two-day offsite, and the budget is tight. A hotel supplier, Lucas, offers meeting rooms and accommodation. You need quotes for ten people, with shared double rooms and one meeting room. Write to him formally to ask for a group rate and the conditions.
tasks: Introduce your request for a two-day offsite for ten people in Turkey.
Ask for a quote with shared double rooms, one meeting room and a group discount.
Request the cancellation conditions and a reply by next Wednesday.

situation: You are talking to a supplier in the UK, Elena, about keeping a consignment stock of a critical raw material for a paediatric suspension. She is worried about carrying the cost. You want to explain that you will share a rolling forecast and agree a minimum volume, so the risk is limited. Make her feel reassured.
tasks: Explain why you want Elena to hold a consignment stock of the critical item.
Reassure her by offering a rolling forecast and a minimum volume commitment.
Suggest a call next week to agree the figures and the payment terms.

situation:
You attended a meeting with Hannah Reyes' team after a tender customer in India asked for a written assurance of supply for the next twelve months of a respiratory product. Your notes are below. Write a follow-up email to Hannah.
- customer needs letter by 20 Nov
- supply plan covers 95 percent of tender volume
- gap of 5 percent in Q2, needs second line
- Hannah to draft letter, Alex to check volumes
- legal review needed before sending
- next call Friday 10:00
tasks: Summarise the customer's request and what the supply plan covers, including the five percent gap.
List actions with owners and dates for the letter, the volume check and the legal review.
Ask Hannah to confirm the 20 November deadline and flag the open question about the second line.

situation: Your project for an active ingredient in South Africa ends next month, and run-state support goes to the operations team. You need your manager Lucas Nair to approve a two-week overlap, during which you remain available for questions. Ask for his approval and explain what you will deliver in that period.
tasks: Ask Lucas to approve a two-week overlap period after the project ends.
List what you will hand over, such as documents, system access and open issues.
Request his decision by Friday so you can schedule training for the operations team.

situation: You negotiated a penalty-free window with a supplier in Ireland, which means you can revise the forecast for a respiratory product once in the next two months without extra charges. Sofia Ahmed, the supplier's account manager, helped to agree it. Tell her you are grateful, summarise the terms and explain when you will send the revision. Sound reassuring.
tasks: Thank Sofia for agreeing a penalty-free window for one forecast revision.
Summarise the terms, including the two-month period and the single revision.
State when you plan to send the updated forecast and promise to share it early.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, our finance team needs the oncology infusion demand figures two days earlier than planned, so can we bring the demand review forward from Thursday to Tuesday? I understand it is short notice. We can send the pre-read today. Best wishes, Tom Fischer" Tom is a supplier contact in Australia. Reply formally.
tasks: Confirm that you can move the demand review from Thursday to Tuesday, or propose a different time.
Ask Tom to send the pre-read today, and name the data you want in it.
Mention one condition, such as the supplier confirming attendance, and close politely.

situation: Your request for travel budget to visit a supplier site in Brazil for a quality audit was refused last week without a clear reason. Laura Larsen, a peer who controls the shared budget, said the funds were gone. You are disappointed because the audit was part of the corrective plan for a vial-based injectable. Ask for an explanation and an alternative.
tasks: Say you were disappointed that the travel budget for the supplier audit in Brazil was refused.
Explain that the audit belongs to the corrective plan for the vial-based injectable.
Ask Laura for the reason and for another way to fund the visit this quarter.

situation: An out-of-specification result appeared in a retained sample of an active ingredient in South Africa. You think a retest is needed before anyone decides about the batch. Your manager, Laura Rossi, must authorise the retest and the extra cost. Ask her for approval and explain what you will do in the meantime. Keep it neutral.
tasks: Report the out-of-specification result found in the retained sample of the active ingredient.
Request approval for a retest and say what it would cost or require.
Say that the batch will stay on hold until the retest result arrives.

situation: A supplier has offered a ten percent discount on an oral solid dose tablet, but only if you raise the minimum order quantity from 50,000 to 200,000 units. Katarina, a peer in procurement in Turkey, accepted this offer in principle. You think it creates too much inventory risk. Write to her formally.
tasks: Explain your concern about raising the minimum order from 50,000 to 200,000 units.
Compare the ten percent discount with the cost of holding extra stock.
Ask Katarina to pause the acceptance until you share a scenario by Thursday.

situation: A supplier in Australia moved its dispatch date for device sub-assemblies twice this month without telling anyone, and your team heard about it only when the truck did not arrive. You want your manager Mei to speak to the supplier's director. Ask for her help in a friendly way.
tasks: Explain that the supplier moved the dispatch date twice without telling anyone.
Describe how this affected your team, giving the dates the truck did not arrive.
Ask Mei to raise the issue with the supplier's director and agree a notice rule.

situation: You depend on one supplier in Egypt for a cardiovascular tablet, and you would like a second supplier approved to reduce this risk. Mei Costa works at the current supplier and could share the technical documents your team needs. Write formally to ask for her cooperation and explain that this is not a criticism.
tasks: Explain that you want to approve a second supplier to reduce single-source risk.
Make clear that this is not a criticism of the current supplier's performance.
Ask Mei to share the technical documents by the end of the month.

situation: A promotion in one country was not shared with the planning team, and it will drain the stock of an oncology infusion faster than expected. Samir Petrov, your contact at a customer in South Africa, ordered based on the old plan. Tell him about the problem, what you are doing and what happens next. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Samir about the unannounced promotion and say that it will use up stock faster.
Explain what you are doing, such as redirecting stock, to protect his orders.
Say you will update him on Monday and ask him to share any known order changes.

situation:
You joined a call with Oliver Tanaka after a customer in Singapore received the wrong pack size of a cold-chain biologic and asked for an immediate replacement. Your notes are below. Write the follow-up email to Oliver.
- customer received 10-vial packs, ordered 5-vial
- 6 pallets affected, in cold room
- replacement ships Tuesday by air
- Oliver to approve air freight cost
- Alex to inform the customer today
- root cause check by quality by 30 Nov
tasks: Summarise what went wrong with the pack size and how many pallets are affected.
List the actions with owners and dates, including air freight approval and the customer message.
Ask Oliver to confirm the replacement plan and flag the open root cause question.

situation:
You met Priya Silva to prepare a delegation visit to your warehouse in Canada, where oncology infusions are stored. Your notes are below. Write her a friendly follow-up email.
- visit on 14 Nov, 12 people
- safety briefing at 09:00, helmets and vests
- route: dock, cold room, packing area
- cold room visit limited to 6 people at a time
- Alex to send agenda by Friday
tasks: Summarise the visit plan, including date, group size and the safety briefing time.
Describe the route through the warehouse and the limit for the cold room.
Confirm your action to send the agenda by Friday and ask Priya for the participant list.

situation: A wholesaler in Egypt says three deliveries of an inhaler in a row arrived short, and it is now threatening to switch to another company. Priya Nair, a peer in warehouse operations, packed those orders. You are disappointed that the earlier warnings were not acted on. Write to her and ask for facts and a quick fix.
tasks: Describe the three short deliveries to the wholesaler and the risk of losing the customer.
Say you are disappointed that earlier warnings did not lead to action.
Ask Priya for the picking records and a correction plan by Wednesday.

situation:
You met Mei Tanaka to ask for extra budget to hire a temporary planner for the peak season of a paediatric suspension in Canada. Your notes are below. Write the follow-up email to Mei.
- peak season October to January
- need one planner, 3 months
- cost 24,000 CAD, not in budget
- workload up 30 percent since June
- Mei to check with finance by 8 Nov
- Alex to send job description by Friday
- decision at the next budget meeting
tasks: Summarise the request for a temporary planner and the reasons, including the workload increase.
List the actions with owners and dates for finance, the job description and the budget meeting.
Ask Mei to confirm the notes and say what you will do if the budget is refused.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the wholesaler in Singapore told us that three deliveries of the cold-chain biologic arrived short in a row, and they may switch supplier. I need to speak to their director on Thursday. Can you give me the facts and a plan? Thanks, Kenji Novak" Kenji is your manager. Reply in a friendly but precise way.
tasks: Thank Kenji and summarise the facts about the three short deliveries you have so far.
Explain the likely cause, and the immediate action to fill the missing quantities.
Offer a short briefing before Thursday's conversation with the director and give a time.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Last month's forecast accuracy for an oral solid dose tablet in Brazil dropped to 71 percent, below the 80 percent target, because one tender order of 400,000 packs was never flagged in advance. You are updating your manager, Rahul Moreau, on what happened and what you will change. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Open by saying why you are writing and give the accuracy figure against the target.
Explain that a single unannounced tender order caused the miss and show what accuracy looks like without it.
Describe the two checks you will add to catch large orders earlier and offer a short call.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A colleague in South Africa ran a three-week price promotion on a prefilled pen without telling planning, and current stock will cover only about ten days of the new demand. You need Daniel Reyes, who leads the regional commercial team, to share the promotion details today so you can reallocate stock. Be polite but make the urgency clear.
tasks: Say you are writing about the South Africa promotion that planning only discovered this week.
Ask for the promotion dates, expected volumes and price mechanics by end of day Thursday.
Explain that without these numbers you cannot protect other markets, and propose a short call tomorrow.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Brazil's peak season for a paediatric suspension starts in six weeks, and you have asked finance for budget to hire a temporary planner for three months. You are telling your peer Rahul, who runs supply planning for the neighbouring site, that the request is submitted and what it means for his team. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that you have submitted a budget request for a temporary planner covering the peak season.
Give the cost, the duration and the workload that justifies the extra headcount.
Explain what happens next and ask whether Rahul's team can support the request in the review.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I saw that a competitor launched a generic version in Canada last week. For the secondary packaging component of our mature product, I think we should cut the forecast by around 15 percent from July. Can you check the open purchase orders and tell me what we could still cancel before the supplier's freeze date on the 20th? Please reply before our Thursday meeting. Thanks, Oliver" Reply to Oliver with your findings and a recommendation. Keep a neutral tone.
tasks: Confirm that you agree to reduce the forecast by about 15 percent from July.
Answer his question by saying which open purchase orders can still be cancelled before the freeze on the 20th.
Promise a revised forecast before Thursday's meeting and suggest who else should be informed.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A competitor's launch in the UK is expected to cut demand for a mature product by roughly 15 percent, which affects a device sub-assembly you order every month. You want your peer Oliver Nair in procurement to check which orders are still flexible. Stay friendly and informal.
tasks: Say hello and explain that the forecast for the device sub-assembly is dropping by about 15 percent.
Ask Oliver which open orders can still be reduced or delayed without penalties.
Suggest a quick catch-up this week and thank him for his help.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. For a prefilled pen sold in South Africa, one supplier provides the only approved needle component, and two outages this year left you short. You have asked Fatima, the account manager, three times for the documents needed to qualify a second supplier, and nothing has arrived. You want her to fix this and understand why it matters to your business. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State that you are following up on the documents needed to approve a second supplier.
Describe the two outages this year and the risk of relying on a single source.
Request the missing documents by a specific date and say what you will do if they do not arrive.

situation:
You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You attended a meeting with Laura Larsen, a peer in the Australian warehouse team, about an inhaler supplier that keeps sending partial shipments. You now need to send a follow-up email. Your notes:
- Last four deliveries arrived in two or three parts each
- Goods receipt takes double time, stock shows wrong availability
- Laura to ask supplier for one consolidated shipment per order, by 14 March
- You to flag partial deliveries in the planning system from next week
- Open point: who pays extra receiving hours
tasks: Open the email by thanking Laura and summarising the problem with partial shipments in one sentence.
List the actions with owners and dates, including Laura's request to the supplier and your system flag.
Flag the open point about receiving costs and ask Laura to confirm the notes are correct.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The monthly S&OP review for an oral solid dose tablet in Canada was set for Tuesday, but the regional lead is travelling and cannot join. You are writing to your manager, Katarina Fischer, to say the meeting should move to Thursday at 10:00 and ask her to approve. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Explain that you are writing about the S&OP review and that the regional lead cannot attend on Tuesday.
Propose Thursday at 10:00 as the new slot and say who you have already checked with.
Ask Katarina to confirm and say you will send the updated invitation and pre-read.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A transport vendor moving an active ingredient to Japan has proposed sending service-level reports every quarter instead of every month. You are telling your peer Fatima Fischer, who worries about losing visibility, that you are negotiating to keep the monthly cycle. Be reassuring.
tasks: Say that you know the vendor suggested quarterly service-level reports and that you share her concern.
Explain that you will insist on monthly reports and why late delivery data hurts planning.
Tell Fatima what you will do next and when you will update her.

situation:
You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The owner of the safety-stock review for clinical-supply kits in Singapore is moving to a new role next week, and the notes are spread across several files. You met with your manager Sofia to agree the handover and must now send a recap. Your notes:
- Review owner changes from Mark to you on 3 November
- Mark to collect all spreadsheets in one shared folder by Friday
- Current safety stock covers 6 weeks, target is 8
- Three kits have unclear service targets, to confirm with clinical team
- Monthly review stays on the second Tuesday
- You to rebuild the calculation file by 15 November
- Open point: budget for extra stock
tasks: Thank Sofia and summarise the decision that you take over the safety-stock review from 3 November.
List the actions with owners and dates, including Mark's folder and your rebuilt file.
Ask Sofia to confirm the notes and raise the budget question as the open point.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. You are organising a two-day team offsite in Sweden for the respiratory product group, and the other region's coordinator, Mark Fischer, booked a hotel at 190 euros per night, far above the agreed limit of 140. The deadline for free cancellation is Friday. You need him to change the booking. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say you are writing about the hotel booked for the Sweden offsite.
Point out that the rate of 190 euros per night is above the agreed 140 euro limit.
Ask him to rebook or negotiate before Friday's cancellation deadline and offer to help with alternatives.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. Printed packaging components for a paediatric suspension in Mexico will reach the plant on Wednesday, two days after the filling slot starts, so the line would sit idle. You are informing your peer Rahul in production planning and want to agree a plan. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State the problem: the packaging arrives on Wednesday and the filling slot begins on Monday.
Say what the delay means for the line and which batch is affected.
Propose moving the slot or filling another product first, and ask for his view by tomorrow.

situation:
You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You attended a meeting with Daniel Ahmed, a peer in the Japanese regional team, about moving a cold-chain biologic planning process from central planning to Japan. You must send a formal follow-up. Your notes:
- Japan team takes over monthly demand review from 1 April
- Central team provides training in two sessions, 12 and 19 March
- Daniel to name a backup planner by 8 March
- Templates and history move to shared folder by 15 March
- Open point: who signs off the final forecast
tasks: Thank Daniel for the meeting and state the decision to transfer the process to Japan from 1 April.
Summarise the training dates, the backup planner and the template move with owners and deadlines.
Raise the sign-off question as an open point and ask Daniel to confirm the notes.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A reorganisation in Germany means your forecast analysis for a prefilled pen, about 60 percent complete, must pass to a colleague on Monday. You are writing to your manager, Ingrid Hall, to say what is done, what remains and where the files are. Use a formal tone.
tasks: Explain that because of the reorganisation you are handing over the unfinished forecast analysis on Monday.
Describe what is complete, what remains and the main assumptions that need review.
Say where the files are stored and offer a handover meeting before you leave the project.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, thank you for your proposal to reduce the lead time of the packaging component from 12 weeks to 8 weeks. At the moment we can offer 10 weeks, because our printing plant in Durban is fully booked until June. If you agree to a six-month volume commitment of 200,000 units, we could review 8 weeks from July. Please let us know by Friday. Kind regards, Rahul" Reply to Rahul in a formal tone.
tasks: Thank Rahul for the offer of ten weeks and say whether you accept it as a first step.
Respond to the six-month volume commitment of 200,000 units and state what you can commit to.
Confirm you will answer by Friday and propose a review of eight weeks from July.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The quarterly business review with the supplier of a paediatric suspension in Egypt falls on the same day as a site audit, so it must be postponed by one week. You are telling your manager, Daniel, which date you propose and what you still need from him. Use a neutral tone.
tasks: Explain that the supplier review clashes with the audit and must move by a week.
Propose the new date and say that you will contact the supplier once Daniel agrees.
Ask whether Daniel wants to add any topics to the agenda before you send the new invitation.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A change control for a prefilled pen made in Egypt was implemented on the line before final quality approval, and a batch is waiting for release. You need Chloe, who leads quality in the other region, to confirm the impact and the timeline for approval today. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Say you are writing about the change control that went live before final quality approval.
Ask Chloe to state the quality impact on the batch waiting for release and the expected approval date.
Explain that the batch is needed for shipment next week and ask for an answer by tomorrow noon.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, we received your complaint about the clinical-supply kit labels. You are right that the expiry date appears as MM/DD/YYYY instead of DD/MM/YYYY on 1,200 kits sent to Poland. We can reprint within five working days, or send replacement labels for your team to apply. Which option do you prefer? We also need the lot numbers confirmed. Best regards, Samir" Reply to Samir in a neutral tone.
tasks: Thank Samir for acknowledging the error and say which option you prefer, reprint or replacement labels.
Confirm the lot numbers and the number of affected kits.
State the date by which you need the corrected labels so the shipment is not delayed.

situation:
You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. An urgent site visit in Turkey overlaps with a stakeholder workshop planned for months, and you met with your manager Julia to decide what to do. You now send a formal follow-up. Your notes:
- Site visit to the packaging plant stays on 9 and 10 April
- Workshop moves to 23 April, same room
- You to send new invitations by Monday
- Julia to inform the regional director personally
- Open point: whether the external facilitator is free on 23 April
tasks: Open by confirming the decision to keep the site visit and move the workshop.
Summarise the new date and the actions with owners and deadlines.
Ask Julia to confirm and flag the facilitator's availability as the open point.

situation:
You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You joined a call with your manager Laura Reyes about a standard template for demand-review notes that will be used across all regions. You must send a friendly follow-up. Your notes:
- One template for all regions from the May cycle
- Sections: assumptions, risks, decisions, actions
- Australia pilots it in April
- You to share a draft by 20 March
- Laura to approve final version by 5 April
- Open point: do small markets need a shorter version?
tasks: Thank Laura for the call and say what was agreed about the new template.
Summarise the sections, the April pilot in Australia and the actions with owners and dates.
Ask Laura to confirm the notes and give her view on a shorter version for small markets.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A deviation affecting clinical-supply kits in Australia was closed four days later than agreed, and the release date for a trial shipment is now at risk. You are writing to your peer Hannah in quality, who owned the closure, and you feel let down. Be disappointed but professional.
tasks: Say you are writing about the deviation that closed four days after the agreed date.
Explain the effect on the trial shipment's release date and the pressure it creates.
Ask Hannah what caused the delay and how closure dates will be protected in future.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. An excipient lot needed for an active ingredient is nine days late because of a raw-material shortage at the supplier's plant. You are writing formally to Sofia Novak, who manages the sister plant in Singapore, to ask whether she can lend 300 kilograms from her stock. Use a formal tone.
tasks: Explain that the excipient lot is nine days late due to a raw-material shortage at the supplier.
Ask Sofia whether her site can lend 300 kilograms and say when you need it.
Offer to return the quantity when the late lot arrives and ask for her reply by Wednesday.

situation: You are a customer service planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear team, our hospital tender for the inhaler runs for twelve months from August. After the shortage in January, we need written assurance of supply for the full period, with monthly volumes of about 4,000 units. Please send this by Friday. Regards, Carlos Brandt, Procurement Manager" Reply to Carlos with an apology and explain what you can commit to.
tasks: Apologise sincerely for the shortage in January and the trouble it caused.
Confirm the monthly volume of 4,000 units and say what you can assure in writing.
Tell Carlos when the formal letter will arrive and offer a call with the supply team.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, the quarterly review for the Australia tablet range is cancelled this week because the director is unavailable. We will replace it with a written update. Could you send your forecast summary and the two risks you wanted to discuss by Tuesday? Thanks, Elena" Reply to Elena. Apologise because you had not finished the summary and your numbers will arrive late.
tasks: Acknowledge that the review is cancelled and that a written update replaces it.
Apologise that the forecast summary is not ready and give the day you can send it.
Briefly mention the two risks you wanted to discuss and ask whether Elena prefers them in the same document.

situation: You are a supply planning lead at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I received your request to fund an APICS planning certification for two of your team members. The training budget for Singapore is tight this year, so I can approve only one place of about 1,800 dollars. Could you tell me who should go first and why? Best, Elena" Reply to Elena. Be firm but polite: you want both places, justify them and offer a compromise.
tasks: Thank Elena for the offer of one place and explain that you still hope to fund both.
Give the business reason for certifying both planners and the benefit to forecast quality.
Propose a compromise, such as staggering the second place into next quarter, and ask for a decision this week.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, a colleague from finance, Mei, will join your supply planning team on 1 December. She has no planning background. Could you send me a rough first-month plan and tell me who will be her mentor? Thanks, Hannah" Reply to Hannah in a friendly way and explain how you will welcome Mei.
tasks: Thank Hannah and say you are happy Mei is joining the team.
Outline a first-month plan with a few key topics, such as the cardiovascular tablet basics and system training.
Name the mentor and say when you will send the detailed plan.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, our commercial forecast for the packaging component is 40 percent above your statistical forecast for both October and November. Sales in Ireland expects a new tender. I need you to use the commercial numbers in the plan. Can we agree today? Nadia" Reply to Nadia. Be firm but polite: you will not simply adopt the commercial numbers without evidence.
tasks: Acknowledge Nadia's point about the new tender in Ireland and the 40 percent gap.
Explain that you need evidence, such as tender status and volumes, before changing the plan.
Propose a compromise, such as a risk scenario for October and November, and a review date.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A transport vendor moving secondary packaging components in Turkey has proposed to send service-level reports every quarter instead of every month. You are writing to your manager, Ingrid, to complain about the proposal and ask her to support insisting on monthly reports. Use a formal tone.
tasks: Say you are writing about the vendor's proposal to move service-level reports to a quarterly cycle.
Explain why three-month reporting delays problem detection and harms planning.
Ask Ingrid to back the request for monthly reports in the next contract meeting.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A contractor will cover a maternity leave for diabetes products in Germany from 2 February for six months. You want Julia Petrov, a colleague in the other region who did the same job last year, to share her onboarding material and give an hour of her time. Stay friendly.
tasks: Introduce the situation: a contractor starts on 2 February to cover a maternity leave.
Ask Julia to share her onboarding checklist and any useful process documents.
Request one hour in the first week to answer questions and thank her.

situation:
You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You attended a meeting with your manager Daniel about a competitor's launch in Japan that lowers the forecast for a mature cardiovascular tablet by about 15 percent. You must send a formal follow-up. Your notes:
- New baseline is 15 percent lower from September
- You to update the forecast in the system by 5 August
- Daniel to inform finance about revenue impact
- Stock above 12 weeks to be reviewed in the August S&OP
- Open point: should the launch be treated as permanent?
tasks: Summarise the decision to lower the baseline by about 15 percent from September.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the system update and the finance notification.
Flag the open question about whether the competitor effect is permanent and ask Daniel to confirm.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, the stockpiling that inflated paediatric suspension sales in Spain during 2021 has clearly disappeared. I suggest we reset the baseline using only the last 18 months. Do you agree? I would also like your view on whether to keep the seasonal factors. Best regards, Andre" Reply to Andre in a formal tone.
tasks: State whether you agree to reset the baseline using only the last eighteen months of data.
Give your opinion on the seasonal factors and the reason for your view.
Propose a date to implement the new baseline and ask Andre to share his analysis.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A cold-chain biologic launches in Brazil in three weeks, but the ocean shipment is delayed. You need your manager Julia Lindqvist to approve air freight, which costs about 38,000 dollars more. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Explain that the ocean shipment of the biologic is delayed and the Brazilian launch is in three weeks.
State the extra cost of air freight and what it protects, such as first orders.
Ask Julia to approve by Wednesday so you can book the flight and mention the alternative.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A supplier delay on an ingredient for a paediatric suspension will not affect this month's output in Chile, but it will use all the safety stock planned for next month. You are writing to Marta Hall, your peer in procurement, because you were told the delivery was safe. Be disappointed but professional.
tasks: Say you are writing about the ingredient delay and that it empties next month's safety stock.
Remind Marta that you had been told the delivery date was secure and explain the impact.
Ask her to press the supplier for a firm date and share weekly updates until it arrives.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. About 12,000 euros of your respiratory product budget in Sweden were left unused in the third quarter because of a delayed order, and finance's rules do not allow carry-over. You want to complain to your manager, Rahul, that the rule is unfair here and ask him to request an exception. Use a formal tone.
tasks: State that you are writing about the unused 12,000 euros and the rule against carrying budget over.
Explain that the order was delayed by the supplier and the money is still needed next quarter.
Ask Rahul to request an exception from finance before the quarter closes.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A supplier of a cold-chain biologic component in Ireland has offered a 9 percent discount, but only if you raise the minimum order quantity from 5,000 to 20,000 units. You are asking Julia Silva, the account manager, whether a middle option is possible. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Thank Julia for the discount offer and say that you are writing to discuss the minimum order quantity.
Explain that 20,000 units is too high for your demand and expiry constraints.
Ask whether a minimum of 10,000 units or a staged discount is possible and request an answer in a week.

situation:
You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. You spoke with Andre Fischer, a transport supplier in Egypt, about moving the delivery of a prefilled pen from Friday to Monday because the receiving dock is closed. You now send a friendly recap. Your notes:
- Delivery moves from Friday 14 to Monday 17
- Receiving dock closed Friday for maintenance
- Driver arrives between 8:00 and 10:00
- Andre to confirm the new slot with the carrier by Thursday
- You to update the warehouse team today
- Temperature logger stays active over the weekend
- Open point: weekend parking fee
tasks: Thank Andre for the call and confirm the delivery has moved from Friday to Monday.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the driver's arrival window and the logger.
Raise the parking fee as an open point and ask Andre to confirm the plan.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi! I'm so happy to visit your site in Dublin from 3 to 7 March. I need an invitation letter for my visa, and I haven't booked flights yet. Should I arrive Sunday or Monday morning? Also, is there a hotel you recommend near the site? Thanks, Andre" Reply to Andre in a friendly way.
tasks: Welcome Andre and say you will send the visa invitation letter this week.
Advise whether to arrive on Sunday or Monday morning and explain why.
Recommend a hotel near the site and say when you will share the visit agenda.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A regional analyst in Egypt works about half of the time on respiratory products and half on another department's reports. You want your peer Rahul Kowalski to agree to split her cost 50-50 between your two departments and need his view before you speak to finance. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain your idea of sharing the analyst's cost equally between your two departments.
Give the reason, such as the analyst's workload split of roughly half and half.
Ask Rahul for his opinion by Friday and suggest a short call to agree the next step.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear team, the stock-out of the oral solid dose tablet at our key account in India lasted eleven days and they are furious. I need a written recovery plan by Thursday with dates, quantities and what we will do to prevent a repeat. Please also tell me if expedited freight is needed. Hannah" Reply to your manager Hannah Hall in a formal tone with your plan.
tasks: Acknowledge the stock-out and confirm you will deliver the written recovery plan by Thursday.
Summarise the recovery steps with dates and quantities, and say whether expedited freight is required.
Describe the measures to prevent a repeat and offer a status meeting.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A new demand planner for vial-based injectables in Brazil starts on Monday and you will be her buddy. You are writing formally to your peer Elena Brandt, who manages the system access team, to ask for a laptop and planning system access to be ready by Monday morning. Use a formal tone.
tasks: Explain that a new demand planner starts on Monday and that you will act as buddy.
Request the laptop and access to the planning system and shared folders before 9:00 on Monday.
Ask Elena who to contact if anything is missing and thank her for the support.

situation: You are a supply planner at a pharmaceutical company. A change control for a secondary packaging component in Italy was implemented before final quality approval, and your peer Daniel in operations signed off the start. You think this was a process failure that could delay a shipment. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Say you are writing about the change control implemented before final quality approval.
Describe the risk to the shipment and the possible need to hold the affected lots.
Ask Daniel to explain how it happened and agree a step to stop it repeating.

situation:
You chaired a short call with Katarina, a planning peer in Chile, about the weekly exception-based routine for a diabetes product that starts next month. Your notes are below.
- Start Monday 2 November, 30 minutes every week
- Review only items outside tolerance: cover under 3 weeks or forecast gap over 15 percent
- Katarina sends the exception list by Friday noon
- You keep the action log; Chile pilots first for 4 weeks
- Review of the pilot on Monday 30 November
- Open point: who covers the list when Katarina is on leave?
Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Thank Katarina for her time and say you are summarising the call on the new weekly routine.
Summarise the decisions and list the actions with owners and dates, including the Friday noon deadline.
Flag the open point about leave cover and ask her to confirm the notes by Wednesday.

situation: Daniel is a planner in Poland who works with you on a cold-chain biologic. The new weekly exception-based planning routine starts next month, but the thresholds he circulated on Tuesday contradict the agreed template, and the dry run is on Thursday. You need him to correct the file before then. Keep the tone neutral and factual.
tasks: Open by naming the file Daniel circulated on Tuesday and explain why you are writing.
Point out the two thresholds that differ from the agreed template and describe the effect on the dry run.
Ask him to send a corrected version by Wednesday evening and offer a short call.

situation: Amira Silva works at a contract manufacturer in Germany that fills a diabetes product for your team. Their cleaning verification record for line 3 arrived with the second signature missing, so the line must be re-checked before the next batch is released on Friday. You depend on that release for the week's shipments. Be polite but make the urgency clear.
tasks: Explain that the cleaning verification record for line 3 is incomplete and name the missing signature.
Request a re-check of the line and the completed record by Thursday noon.
Ask her to confirm the new timeline and warn that Friday's release depends on it.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I saw your leave request for 9 to 20 March. Who will cover the respiratory product while you are away? The monthly supply review is on 12 March, and I need the safety-stock numbers for India before then. Please also tell me which escalations might come up. Thanks, Andre Silva." Reply to Andre and settle the cover for your leave. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Name the colleague who will cover your respiratory product and confirm the handover date.
Answer his concern about the 12 March supply review and the India safety-stock numbers.
List the escalations that may arise and say how he can reach you in an emergency.

situation: Viktor is a colleague in Brazil who is coming back on Monday after six months away. In that time your team moved the secondary packaging component planning to a new weekly template and a different approval step. You want to meet him on his first day to bring him up to date. Stay friendly.
tasks: Welcome Viktor back and say you would like to walk him through what changed.
Describe the two main changes, the new weekly template and the extra approval step.
Propose a 45-minute session on Monday and ask which time suits him.

situation: Your supplier delivered only 12,000 of the 24,000 glass vials ordered for a secondary packaging line, and gave no date for the rest. Hannah Reyes plans the filling schedule in Canada and relies on those vials. Tell her what happened, what you have asked the supplier, and when you will update her next. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State that only half of the vial order arrived and give the quantities delivered and missing.
Explain what you have asked the supplier and that no date has been confirmed yet.
Tell Hannah when you will send the next update and what she can plan with meanwhile.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, our new policy now requires a second check before any manual forecast override. I noticed you changed the UK volume for next quarter on Monday without it. Could you explain why and let me know who will sign it off? We need this closed by Friday. Best regards, Ingrid." Reply to Ingrid. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain why you changed the UK volume for next quarter on Monday.
Accept or challenge her point about the missing second check and name who will sign it off.
Commit to closing the check by Friday and say how overrides will be handled in future.

situation: Chloe Ruiz, your peer in Australia, promised to book the two-day visit to a supplier's site next month for a clinical-supply kit, but three weeks later you still have no flights, hotel or site agenda. The supplier needs names for security by the 15th. Raise the problem and ask her to sort it out. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Say you are writing about the supplier visit next month and that nothing has been confirmed yet.
Describe what is missing, the bookings, the agenda and the names for site security.
Ask Chloe for a status by Wednesday and propose splitting the tasks if she is overloaded.

situation: Last month forecast accuracy for an oral solid dose tablet in Japan dropped to 71 percent against a target of 85, mainly because of one unexpected order of 400,000 tablets. Your manager Yuki wants a clear view. You are not blaming anyone, but you want it known that the process gave no early warning. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Open by stating the accuracy figure, the target and the single order behind the miss.
Explain why the order was not visible in the forecast and where the process failed to warn you.
Ask Yuki to agree an early-warning rule with sales and propose a date to review it.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, a distributor in Milan told me they received a back-order for the prefilled pen on 3 October with no warning. They want a formal explanation by Thursday, otherwise they will escalate. Can you give me the facts and a short text I can forward? Thanks, Andre Lindqvist." Reply to Andre as a helpful peer. Stay friendly.
tasks: Acknowledge the distributor's complaint about the unannounced back-order on 3 October.
Give the facts, the cause of the shortfall and the new delivery date.
Offer a short paragraph he can forward and promise it before Thursday.

situation: Julia Tanaka manages a supplier of an active ingredient and delivers to your Brazil site. Next month a pilot of automatic safety-stock recalculation starts in two countries, which may slightly change your order sizes. You want her to hear it from you first. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Julia that a pilot of automatic safety-stock recalculation starts next month in two countries.
Explain what may change for her, such as order sizes and the timing of purchase orders.
Say you will share the first results after four weeks and invite her questions.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I know the kick-off for the inhaler project is Tuesday at 3 pm, but our team in Johannesburg can't stay for three hours. Could we split it into two sessions? Maybe the technical part first. Let me know what works. Priya." Reply to Priya, the supplier contact, and agree a new format. Stay friendly.
tasks: Agree to split the kick-off into two shorter sessions and thank Priya for raising it.
Propose which topics go in each session and suggest two possible dates.
Ask her to confirm the attendees and say you will send updated invitations.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Alex, the tracker shows a reading of 11 degrees for about 40 minutes on pallet 7 of the biologic shipment to Montreal. Quality wants to quarantine all 6 pallets until a decision is taken. What is your view and what do you propose? I need it before noon. Kenji." Reply to your manager Kenji. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Give your view on whether the other five pallets should be quarantined or released.
Propose next steps for pallet 7 and name who must provide the stability data.
State what you need from Kenji, and the time by which you will report back.

situation: Ingrid Okafor is a customer contact in Turkey. An urgent site visit you must make on Wednesday now overlaps with the stakeholder workshop on vial-based injectables that you planned months ago. You want to move the workshop to the following Monday and keep her on side. Be polite but make clear it is urgent.
tasks: Apologise for the clash and explain that an urgent site visit on Wednesday has come up.
Propose moving the workshop to the following Monday and offer one backup date.
Ask Ingrid to confirm by tomorrow so you can update the other participants.

situation: A senior director at a customer asked for a call with your management after repeated delays on a cold-chain biologic. Tom, your peer who owns the logistics plan in India, did not tell you about the third delay until the customer complained. You want better communication. Sound disappointed but stay professional.
tasks: Explain that the customer director has asked for a call with management after repeated delays.
Say you learned about the third delay only from the customer, and explain the impact on you.
Ask Tom to share delay information the same day and suggest a daily check-in until it is resolved.

situation: Finance has moved its deadline, so the demand review you share with Samir in South Africa must happen on Wednesday instead of Friday. Samir hasn't updated the diabetes product baseline yet, and he may resist the change. You need his numbers by Tuesday midday. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say the demand review is moving from Friday to Wednesday because of the finance deadline.
Explain that you need his updated baseline by Tuesday midday and why that matters.
Ask him to tell you today if the new date is impossible so you can find a solution.

situation:
You attended a call with Katarina Okafor from the Turkey team about a device sub-assembly whose supplier moved its dispatch date twice without telling anyone. Your notes are below.
- Dispatch moved from 6 to 13 to 20 November
- No notice was sent either time
- Supplier to send written explanation by Friday
- Katarina to check buffer stock in Istanbul, about 9 days
- You will request a weekly status call
Stay friendly, but be clear about the open actions.
tasks: Thank Katarina for the call and say you are writing to confirm what was agreed.
Summarise the two date changes and list each action with its owner and deadline.
Ask her to confirm the buffer-stock figure and say when you will report back.

situation: A key account in Sweden has demanded a recovery plan after a stock-out of an oral solid dose tablet last week. You are updating your manager, Lucas Brandt, on the plan you have drafted: an expedited batch on 12 November, a split delivery and a daily stock check. You want to reassure him and say what happens next. Sound reassuring.
tasks: Tell Lucas that a recovery plan for the Swedish key account is ready and give its three parts.
Explain the cause of the stock-out and the expected date stock will be back to normal.
State what you need from him to approve the plan and when you will update again.

situation: Two members of your oncology infusion planning team want to take a planning certification that costs about 1,800 euros each. Viktor Silva, a peer in Italy, manages a shared training budget and decides on requests. You want him to approve the funding from the next quarter's allocation. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain that two colleagues would like to take a planning certification and give the total cost.
Say how the course helps the oncology infusion planning work and your team.
Ask Viktor whether the shared training budget can cover it and what he needs from you.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, we heard that a batch of the paediatric suspension failed release. Our hospital group in India only holds two weeks of cover for next quarter. Please confirm what quantity you can deliver and when. We need a written answer for our tender committee by Monday. Regards, Viktor." Reply to Viktor, a customer. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Confirm that a batch failed release and apologise for the uncertainty it causes.
State the quantity you can deliver and the realistic dates, based on the two weeks of cover.
Promise a written commitment before Monday and give a contact for questions.

situation:
An intern joins your planning team for three months. You met Ben Ruiz, who leads the host team in Chile, to agree how the first weeks will work. Your notes are below.
- Starts Monday 9 November, ends 5 February
- Buddy: you, 30 minutes every Friday
- Weeks 1 and 2: learn the respiratory product forecast template
- Week 3: first mini-project on inventory cover
- Final presentation to the team on 28 January
- Laptop and access still pending
Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Ben for the meeting and say you are confirming the plan for the intern's three months.
Summarise the schedule and the mini-project, with owners and dates.
Ask him to chase the laptop and system access and confirm the notes.

situation: OTIF for the main customer in Italy fell to 82 percent against a target of 95, and the account manager has complained loudly. You believe warehouse capacity in September and late supplier deliveries are the main causes, but you have been blamed for it. You want your manager Samir Larsen to help. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say OTIF to this customer dropped to 82 percent and that you understand the account manager's concern.
Explain the two causes you identified and say which are outside planning's control.
Ask Samir to support a joint review with the warehouse and supplier management next week.

situation: A supplier in Turkey keeps sending your diabetes product in several small shipments for one order, so goods receipt takes longer and your planning data is out of date for days. Oliver Rossi, the account contact, asked you to explain what is wrong. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, we ship as soon as units are ready. Is this a problem for you? Oliver." Reply with the issue and a request. Stay neutral.
tasks: Answer Oliver's question: yes, partial shipments cause a problem, and say why.
Describe the effect on goods receipt and planning with one recent example.
Ask the supplier to consolidate shipments or send an advance notice and propose a trial.

situation: A key item for your cardiovascular tablet has a lead time of twelve weeks and your inventory is at only three weeks of cover. You want Hannah Petrov, your supplier contact in Brazil, to hold a consignment stock of 20,000 units at her site that you pay for on use. You need her answer within a week. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that you would like to set up a consignment stock of the critical item.
Give the quantity, the lead-time problem and how invoicing could work on usage.
Ask Hannah for a decision within a week and offer a call to discuss terms.

situation: The owner of the safety-stock review for an active ingredient in Egypt, Yuki Costa, is changing role next month. The notes for the review are scattered across emails and two spreadsheets, and nobody has been named to take over. You are writing to the manager of the team. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that Yuki Costa will change role next month and the safety-stock review needs a new owner.
Describe the gap, with notes spread across emails and two spreadsheets.
Ask for a decision on the new owner by the end of next week and offer to collect the notes.

situation: A logistics provider announced a 6 percent rate increase for inhalers to Sweden, starting in January. Your manager Chloe must decide what to offer back. You have compared two other carriers and a volume discount scenario. Ask her for a mandate to negotiate. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Chloe of the 6 percent rate increase and the date it would take effect.
Summarise your comparison of two other carriers and the volume discount option.
Request approval to negotiate a counter-offer and ask for her limit by Friday.

situation: Your flight to the regional workshop in Milan was cancelled, and the next available seat arrives two hours after the opening session on Tuesday. The workshop covers planning of a paediatric suspension and your input is needed. You are writing to your manager, Samir Okafor, for a decision. Stay neutral.
tasks: Explain that your flight to the workshop was cancelled and the next one lands after the opening.
Offer two options, joining late in person or dialling in for the first session.
Ask Samir to choose and tell him you will rebook by this afternoon.

situation:
You hosted a short planning session with Ingrid about splitting the inhaler kick-off meeting in Brazil into two shorter parts. Your notes are below.
- Session 1: scope and timeline, Tuesday 10 November, 90 minutes
- Session 2: ordering and stock rules, Thursday 12 November, 90 minutes
- Ingrid to send the agenda by 6 November
- You will invite the supplier and warehouse leads
- Maximum 12 participants
- Open: recordings allowed?
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Open by thanking Ingrid for the discussion and stating that you are confirming the outcomes.
Summarise both sessions and list actions with owners and dates.
Flag the open question about recordings and ask for her confirmation by Friday.

situation: A cold-chain data logger stopped recording during a shipment of an active ingredient to Canada, so there is a gap of about six hours in the temperature record. Samir Okafor works in quality in the Canada region. You need his help to decide whether the shipment can be accepted. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Samir that a data logger failed on the active ingredient shipment and describe the gap.
Ask what documents or evidence quality needs to release the shipment.
Request an answer by tomorrow because production planning depends on it.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Alex, you suggested a 90-day payment term to the clinical-kit supplier in exchange for 30 percent more volume. Finance is worried about their reaction. What exactly will you offer, and what is your fallback? Please send me the details before our Thursday call. Kenji." Reply to Kenji. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain exactly what you will offer: the 90-day payment term and the extra annual volume.
Describe your fallback position and why you think the supplier will accept.
Address the finance concern and say you will send details before Thursday.

situation:
You attended a call with Peter Hall, a customer contact in South Africa, because your flight cancellation puts your presence at the regional workshop on inhalers at risk. Your notes are below.
- Your flight on Monday 16 November was cancelled
- Next flight lands 14:30, after the first session
- Peter agrees to move your talk from 09:00 to 15:00
- You send slides by Friday
- Peter's team books the room and sets up the video link
- Fallback: remote talk if no seat is available
- Attendee list to be shared by Thursday
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Peter for his flexibility and confirm the new time for your talk.
Summarise the agreed actions with owners and dates, including the slides and the video link.
Explain the fallback of a remote talk and ask him to confirm all points in writing.

situation: A carrier strike in Europe will delay the inbound active ingredient for your clinical-supply kit by about a week, from 2 to 9 November. Your manager Laura Hall needs to know the effect on clinical sites in Chile and decide whether to approve air freight for part of the quantity, which costs about 8,000 euros. Keep it formal.
tasks: Inform Laura about the strike and the expected one-week delay of the shipment.
Explain the risk to clinical sites in Chile if nothing changes.
Request approval for air freight of part of the quantity and ask for an answer by Wednesday.

situation:
You met Sofia, who manages a supplier in South Africa, to explain that supplier scorecards for the paediatric suspension will be updated monthly instead of quarterly. Your notes are below.
- First monthly scorecard on 5 December
- Metrics: on-time delivery, quality rejects, response time
- Sofia nominates a contact person by 20 November
- Scorecard shared by email, reviewed on a 20-minute call
- No penalties linked for the first three months
- Question open: add lead-time variance?
Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Sofia for the meeting and say you are summarising the change to monthly scorecards.
List the agreed metrics, dates and owners clearly.
Raise the open question on lead-time variance and ask her to confirm her contact person.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I heard that only half of the vials for the injectable arrived and the supplier gave no date for the rest. Our Brazil launch plan depends on them. What is the real situation and what are you doing about it? I'd like to tell the leadership team today. Katarina." Reply to Katarina, your manager. Stay friendly.
tasks: Describe the real situation: how many vials arrived and how many are still missing.
List what you are doing with the supplier, including escalation and alternative sources.
Say what Katarina can tell the leadership team today and when you will update her.

situation: Your weekly one-to-one with Elena, a colleague in Japan responsible for the prefilled pen forecast, is on Thursday at 8 am your time, which no longer works because your team meeting moved. Elena has skipped it three times without notice. You want a new rhythm. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the Thursday slot no longer works for you and mention the missed meetings politely.
Propose a new rhythm, for example every second Tuesday for 30 minutes.
Ask Elena to reply with her preference by Friday and to give notice if she cannot attend.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, a graduate in our rotation programme will join your team for six weeks from 2 November. Could you suggest a first project suitable for her level? Ideally something connected to the device sub-assembly. Please send your proposal by Friday. Kind regards, Peter Moreau." Reply to Peter, your manager. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Peter and confirm the graduate's start date of 2 November.
Propose a first project connected to the device sub-assembly with a clear goal and deliverable.
Explain who will guide her and how progress will be reviewed during the six weeks.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex! The new demand planner starts on Monday and I thought you could be her buddy. She will cover the respiratory product in South Africa. Could you tell me what you would do in her first week? Thanks! Priya Tanaka." Reply to Priya and plan the first week. Stay friendly.
tasks: Accept the buddy role with enthusiasm and thank Priya for asking.
Outline the first week day by day, including systems access and the respiratory product forecast.
Ask what else Priya needs from you before Monday.

situation: A senior director at a customer asked for a call with your management after repeated delays on inhalers to Egypt. Yuki, a peer who knows the account well, could help you prepare, since the call is next Thursday. You need the delivery history and a view on what to promise. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain that a senior director has asked for a call with management about repeated inhaler delays.
Ask Yuki for the delivery history and her view on what the company can promise.
Suggest a 30-minute preparation meeting on Tuesday and ask what time suits her.

situation: Two regions are competing for the same limited batch of inhalers, 40,000 units available on 20 November. Carlos in Canada has asked his logistics team to reserve all of them, although your region's service level has been lower for two months. You want a fair split. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain that two regions are asking for the same 40,000 inhaler batch and name the date.
Point out that your region has had lower service for two months and propose a fair split.
