Ask Carlos to hold the reservation until you speak, and suggest a call on Monday.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, our marketing team plans a promotion in Poland from 15 November, with a 30 percent increase on the packaging component. We did not tell planning, and I now understand you cannot cover it. Can you explain what is possible? Rahul Moreau." Reply to Rahul, your customer contact. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain what volume you can cover from 15 November and the reasons for the limit.
Say that promotions must be shared with planning early and propose a notice period.
Offer a way forward, such as a phased supply, and ask for a decision by Friday.

situation: One strength of a prefilled pen in Italy could run out before the next shipment lands on 18 November, and current stock covers only eleven days. Your manager Mark Lindqvist can approve an air shipment of 5,000 pens. You need his answer by tomorrow. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Tell Mark that the strength may run out in Italy before the shipment arrives on 18 November.
Give the stock cover figure and the cost of the air shipment of 5,000 pens.
Ask for his approval by tomorrow and explain what happens if no decision is made.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A hospital customer in Japan was invoiced for 4,800 inhalers, but only 4,200 were delivered last Thursday, and the customer's buyer has already rejected the invoice twice. The error sits in a billing step owned by your manager's area, and you want your manager to push the finance team to correct it before month-end. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Open by stating that the Japan invoice does not match the 4,200 inhalers actually delivered.
Explain the 600-unit gap and mention that the buyer has already rejected the invoice twice.
Ask your manager to have finance issue a corrected invoice before month-end and confirm the date.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company, and your supplier of a cardiovascular tablet in Australia has sent you a draft renewal. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I have attached the renewal draft for 2027. Prices are unchanged, but we propose to keep the all-or-nothing delivery rule, so each order ships complete or not at all. Could you confirm by Friday whether this works for you? Best regards, Peter Petrov" Reply to Peter, ask for a partial-delivery clause, and keep the tone firm but polite.
tasks: Thank Peter for the draft and confirm you can answer by his Friday deadline.
Explain why the all-or-nothing rule is a problem and propose a clause allowing partial deliveries.
Suggest a short call next week to agree the wording of the clause.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, Egypt has just approved our device for hospital use. Commercial wants me to add 15,000 sub-assemblies to the forecast from March, but I have no sales history to support it. Can you load it as is? I need an answer today. Thanks, Nadia" Reply to Nadia: you cannot load it without evidence, but you want to help. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Acknowledge Nadia's news about the Egypt approval and her request to load 15,000 units from March.
Explain that you cannot load the volume without a documented basis, and name what evidence you need.
Offer a phased alternative and agree when you will review the numbers together.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Your Spanish customer team moved their diabetes-product review call to 7:00 a.m. your time next Tuesday because of a public holiday on their side, and it is the third early call this month. You manage your team's workload, so you want your manager to agree to a fairer arrangement. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the customer call was moved to 7:00 a.m. next Tuesday because of the Spanish holiday.
Point out that this is the third early call this month and affects preparation time.
Ask your manager to approve a later slot or time off in lieu, and request a decision by Monday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Ireland. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, good news: a contractor, Sofia, starts on 3 March to cover Aoife's maternity leave. She knows SAP but not our cardiovascular tablet portfolio. Could you draft a quick ramp-up plan for her first two weeks and tell me what you need from me? Thanks, Tom" Reply to Tom and stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Tom and say you are happy to prepare a two-week ramp-up plan for Sofia.
Outline the plan briefly: week one on portfolio basics and week two on live forecasting tasks.
List what you need from Tom, such as system access and a laptop, by a specific date.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A hospital pharmacy in Italy has complained that its last three deliveries of an active ingredient arrived two to three days after the agreed window, which disrupted compounding. The delays started when the regional warehouse changed carriers in January. You want your manager to raise this with logistics and fix it. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise the pharmacy's complaint about three deliveries arriving after the agreed window.
Link the delays to the carrier change in January and give the dates you have.
Ask your manager to escalate to logistics and agree a recovery plan this week.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. After a reorganisation in Japan, your half-finished forecast analysis for secondary packaging components must pass to Katarina Moreau, who has not seen it before. You are moving to another team on Friday and want a clean handover. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Introduce the reason for the handover and describe what the analysis covers and how far it has progressed.
Ask Katarina for a one-hour walkthrough before Friday and propose two possible times.
List the files and open questions you will send, and offer to answer queries for two weeks.

situation:
You chaired a stock-out risk meeting with your manager about a limited batch of an active ingredient in Italy, which two regions both want. Here are your notes.
- Batch 4471: 2,000 kg available, Italy asks 1,500, Region B asks 1,200
- Italy's hospital tender starts 10 June
- Region B has 3 weeks of cover left
- Decision: split 1,100 kg to Italy, 900 kg to Region B
- Lucas to ask the supplier for an extra 600 kg by 20 May
- You to update the allocation sheet by Wednesday
- Open point: who pays for expedited freight
tasks: Summarise the allocation decision and the reasons behind the 1,100 and 900 kilogram split.
List the actions with owners and dates, including Lucas's request to the supplier.
Flag the open freight-cost question and ask your manager to confirm the allocation.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, daylight saving ends in Europe this weekend, so our Monday planning sync would land at 6:30 a.m. your time in Sydney. Can you keep it there for the next few weeks? We have a lot to cover for the prefilled pen launch. Regards, Mark" Reply to Mark. You cannot start that early every week, and you must be firm but polite.
tasks: Acknowledge the time shift and the importance of the prefilled pen launch discussions.
Explain that 6:30 a.m. in Sydney is not workable every week and propose a later slot.
Offer to rotate the burden, for example alternating early and late slots, and ask Mark to confirm.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Until now, a central team in Dublin ran the monthly supply review for an oncology infusion, but a regional team in Ireland will take it over from next quarter. Rahul Nair leads the receiving team, and you want to know what he needs to be ready for the first cycle in July. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that the supply review for the oncology infusion moves to Rahul's team next quarter.
Ask Rahul which documents, data access and training his team needs before the July cycle.
Propose a first handover meeting date and ask him to name a contact person.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, because of a public holiday here on Thursday, my team asks to move our customer call about the paediatric suspension to 6:00 a.m. your time on Friday. Would that be acceptable? Please let me know by tomorrow. Kind regards, Elena" Reply to Elena. Early start is hard for you, but the call matters. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Elena and acknowledge the Thursday public holiday in South Africa.
Accept the Friday 6:00 a.m. slot, but say that it is an exception and ask for the agenda in advance.
Confirm the attendees and ask her to send an updated calendar invitation.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in India. From next month, the team will run a weekly planning routine that looks only at exceptions, such as items above or below target cover, instead of reviewing every clinical-supply kit. Some planners worry they will miss problems, and your manager has asked how it is going. Keep the tone reassuring.
tasks: Tell your manager that the exception-based weekly routine starts next month and explain the main idea.
Address the concern about missed problems by describing the thresholds and the monthly full check.
Say what happens next, including a pilot run in the last week of this month.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Canada, organising a two-day team offsite where the budget is tight. You have found a hotel near the office with shared rooms at 140 dollars a night, and your manager has been worried about the total cost. You want to report your progress calmly. Keep the tone reassuring.
tasks: Report that you found a hotel near the office at 140 dollars a night with shared rooms.
Give the total estimated cost for the team and show it stays within the budget.
Say what you need next, such as approval to book by Friday, and mention the free cancellation window.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A hospital pharmacy in Mexico has been receiving device sub-assemblies outside the agreed delivery window, and your manager asked for a status report before talking to the customer. Two of the last five shipments were late, mainly because of customs checks. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise the situation, stating that two of the last five shipments missed the agreed window.
Explain the cause, customs checks, and describe the action already taken with the forwarder.
State the next step and the date by which you will report the first on-time shipment.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You want to renegotiate the lead time for a key component of an oncology infusion from twelve weeks to eight, and a peer in the UK procurement team, Viktor, worries it will upset the supplier. You are updating him on your plan. Keep the tone reassuring.
tasks: Tell Viktor that you plan to ask the supplier to cut the lead time from twelve to eight weeks.
Reassure him by explaining the benefit for both sides, such as a firm forecast and fewer rush orders.
Say what happens next, including a call with the supplier next Tuesday, and invite him to join.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Germany. An excipient lot for a cardiovascular tablet will arrive nine days late because the supplier's plant has a raw-material shortage, and the next production slot is on 12 June. Your manager needs to know the impact and what you are doing. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform your manager that the excipient lot is nine days late and give the new expected date.
Explain the effect on the 12 June production slot and the risk to tablet availability.
Describe the mitigation you are checking and say when you will send the next update.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. In the demand review, sales proposed a manual override that adds 20 per cent to the clinical-supply kit forecast for Sweden, but the planning team does not trust it because it has no documented basis. You are informing Yuki Tanaka, a peer in the demand team, of your position. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Tell Yuki that planning has not accepted the 20 per cent override for the Sweden forecast yet.
Explain why: there is no documented basis and past overrides were too high.
Say what happens next and ask Yuki to send the supporting data before the next review.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, the warehouse reports that our inhaler stock in the UK will run out in about ten days. Why did the system not warn us? This is the second time this year. I need an explanation and a plan by Thursday. Regards, Amira Lindqvist" Reply to your manager. You found that the reorder point was set on old demand. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Acknowledge Amira's concern about the ten days of stock left and the second incident this year.
Explain the root cause: the reorder point was based on old demand, so no alert was raised.
Describe the corrective steps, including an urgent replenishment, and promise a plan by Thursday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I noticed yesterday's vial-injectable supply meeting was missing the Stockholm warehouse and quality leads. Did the invite go to the wrong list? We cannot decide on the release plan without them. Please fix it and tell me when we can meet again. Andre Costa" Reply to your manager Andre and keep the tone formal.
tasks: Confirm that the invitation went to an outdated distribution list and apologise for the omission.
Explain that you have corrected the list and ask who else should be added.
Propose a new meeting time on Friday morning and promise to circulate the notes.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, we saw your request to hold consignment stock of the infusion bag at our South African site. We can do it, but we need a minimum commitment of 12 months. Can you confirm the volumes? Regards, Andre Haddad" You missed his earlier email last week. Reply with an apology. Keep the tone apologetic.
tasks: Apologise for the late reply and for missing Andre's earlier message last week.
Respond to the 12-month commitment: confirm the approximate monthly volumes you can share.
Ask for a written proposal on stock levels and costs, and propose a date for a call.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Brazil. The demand review proposed a manual override on the diabetes-product forecast, and your peer Nadia Kowalski, who owns the commercial inputs, entered it without telling planning. You want her to explain it and work with your team in future. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Open by saying you noticed the manual override on the diabetes forecast in this week's demand review.
Explain the concern: planning was not consulted and cannot trace the assumption behind the change.
Ask Nadia to document the basis for the change and to inform planning before future overrides.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Chile. For the last two months, the statistical forecast for a respiratory product has been about 25 per cent below the commercial forecast, and nobody has reconciled them. You want your manager, Yuki Petrov, to step in so that the S&OP meeting can decide on one number. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Describe the gap of roughly 25 per cent between the statistical and commercial forecasts over two months.
Explain the risk if the difference stays unresolved, such as excess stock or shortages before the S&OP meeting.
Ask your manager to arrange a reconciliation session and name the date you need a decision.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A carrier strike has delayed your inbound shipment of active ingredient for a vial-based injectable, which was due from Europe, by about a week, and your Egypt site only has twelve days of cover. You must raise this with the supplier, Mark Nair, who chose the carrier. Express disappointment but stay professional.
tasks: State that the shipment from Europe is about a week late because of the carrier strike.
Explain the impact on your Egypt site, which has only twelve days of cover.
Ask Mark for alternative transport options and a new delivery date by tomorrow.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Chile. Hannah Petrov, a peer, returned this week after six months away, but she keeps using the old forecast template for the vial-based injectable, and the process changed in April. This causes rework for you. Raise it with her without sounding critical. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Welcome Hannah back and explain that the forecast process changed while she was away.
Point out that the old template creates rework and name the new template she should use.
Offer a short walkthrough on a specific day and ask her to resubmit this week's file.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Germany. A batch of inhalers is on hold while quality investigates a deviation, a gap in the batch documentation. Release was planned for Friday. Your manager asked for a short, factual update on what you know so far. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Tell your manager that the batch of inhalers is on hold because of a documentation gap.
Explain what quality is investigating and the earliest likely release date.
Describe the effect on customer orders and say when you will send the next update.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Sweden. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I heard the carrier strike will delay your active ingredient from Europe by about a week. My region was planning to take a share of that batch on 18 June. What does this mean for us, and can we still count on 400 kilograms? Thanks, Nadia Tanaka" Reply to Nadia and keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Confirm the strike delay of about a week and give your revised arrival estimate.
Answer her question about the 400 kilograms and say whether the 18 June plan still holds.
Tell her when you will update her next and ask her to share her minimum need.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Spain. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello! Our team noticed that the supplier moved the dispatch date of the active ingredient twice this month, and no one told us. We have a production run on the 9th. Did you know? Can you find out the real date? Cheers, Fatima Hall" Reply as a friendly colleague.
tasks: Thank Fatima for raising it and admit you only learned about the second change yesterday.
Explain that you will ask the supplier for a confirmed dispatch date before the 9th.
Promise to share the answer by tomorrow and suggest a standing weekly update.

situation:
You attended a call with your colleague Andre Fischer in another region about a key diabetes-product account in Brazil that demands a recovery plan after a stock-out last month. Here are your notes.
- Stock-out lasted nine days, 30 per cent of orders unfilled
- Cause: late forecast update after a tender win
- Air freight of 3,000 packs approved
- Andre to send recovery plan to the customer by Friday
- You to send revised forecast by Wednesday
- Weekly stock check with the account team from next week
Now write the follow-up email to Andre.
tasks: Summarise what went wrong and the agreed recovery steps in the first paragraph.
List each action with its owner and deadline, including the air freight and the revised forecast.
Ask Andre to confirm the plan and mention the weekly stock check as the next step.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A supplier contact in Sweden, Tom Costa, joins your weekly planning call for a vial-based injectable. Daylight saving ends this weekend, so the usual Thursday 15:00 slot will shift by an hour for him, and you want to agree a time that works for both. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Mention that the clocks change this weekend and that the usual Thursday slot will shift for Tom.
Propose a specific new time and an alternative, and explain why they suit both sides.
Ask Tom to confirm by Wednesday so you can update the invitation.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The reorder point for a secondary packaging component was set on old demand, so the system raised no alert and stock in Japan is now down to three weeks. You must tell a planner in another region, Mark, who also uses this component. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Tell Mark that the reorder point for the packaging component was based on old demand.
Explain that no alert appeared and that Japan now holds only three weeks of stock.
Say what you have changed and ask him to check the same setting in his region.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, we heard that you are looking for another source for the inhaler valve. We are the current sole supplier, and we would prefer not to share volumes. Could you explain the reason? Best regards, Fatima" You must be honest about single-source risk. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Thank Fatima for her openness and say the company values the current relationship.
Explain that single-source risk is the reason and that the second source would cover only part of the volume.
Ask for her cooperation with the qualification timeline and propose a meeting in Turkey next month.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Germany. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi! I saw your request for a safety-stock buffer for the respiratory product. Finance worries about the cost, 1.2 million euros of working capital. Can you justify it? I need the case by Monday. Thanks, Carlos" Reply to Carlos, a colleague in another region. Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Carlos and acknowledge the finance concern about the 1.2 million euros.
Justify the buffer with a concrete risk, such as lead-time variability and the cost of a stock-out.
Offer a lower alternative and promise to send the full case by Monday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Egypt. A new demand planner starts on Monday and you have been named her buddy, but you are also covering two product launches this month and have no spare time. You need your manager Peter to adjust expectations. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say you are glad to be the buddy for the new planner who starts on Monday.
Explain that two product launches this month limit your available time to about two hours a day.
Ask Peter to move one of your tasks or share onboarding duties, and request an answer by Friday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A data logger shows that a pallet of oral solid dose tablets, shipped to Italy, went above the allowed temperature for four hours in transit, and the pallet cannot be released until quality decides. You need Katarina in the other region to send the logger data today. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that a pallet of tablets recorded a temperature excursion of about four hours in transit.
Ask Katarina to send the full logger data and the packaging details today.
State why it is urgent: the pallet stays blocked until quality reviews it.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A respiratory-product shipment for a customer in Singapore is held at the border because one customs document, the certificate of origin, is missing. Kenji Silva, the customer's buyer, expected delivery on Wednesday. You want to inform him openly and keep the relationship warm. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Kenji that the shipment is waiting at the border because the certificate of origin is missing.
Say what you are doing to get the document and give the new expected delivery date.
Offer an interim solution, such as a partial shipment, and promise to update him tomorrow.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company in Germany. The licence for your forecasting tool expires in August and your manager Chloe has not yet approved the one-year extension, which is costing you time because the vendor is asking for a decision. You want to press her to decide. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Remind Chloe that the forecasting tool licence expires in August and the extension is still pending.
Explain the risk of a lapse, such as losing history and stopping inhaler forecasts.
Ask for a decision by the end of next week and offer to prepare a cost summary.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A delegation of eight visitors will tour the oncology-infusion warehouse in Egypt on Thursday, and nobody has arranged their safety briefing or a visitor route. Oliver Nair manages the site in the other region. The visit is in two days, so you need his help quickly. Be polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that eight visitors will tour the warehouse on Thursday and no safety briefing is arranged yet.
Ask Oliver to prepare a short briefing and a safe visitor route, and tell you which protective equipment is needed.
Request confirmation by tomorrow noon so you can send the visitors their instructions.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A tender customer in Australia has asked for written assurance that you can supply a cardiovascular tablet for the next twelve months, and your manager Chloe must sign it. You have reviewed the forecast and stock plan and see no major risk. Keep the tone reassuring.
tasks: Tell Chloe that the tender customer wants a written assurance of supply for twelve months.
Summarise the evidence: forecast, inventory plan and the safety stock you hold.
Say what happens next: you will draft the letter and send it to her for signature by Thursday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A delegation will visit the oncology-infusion warehouse in Egypt next Monday, and your manager Katarina asked for a brief status report on the preparations. The route and the safety briefing are ready, but the site has not yet confirmed visitor badges. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Report that the visit is next Monday and the route and safety briefing are ready.
Mention the open item: the site has not yet confirmed visitor badges.
State your next step and the day you will confirm the final arrangements.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, a customer in Brazil received 100 millilitre bottles of the paediatric suspension, but they ordered 60 millilitre packs. They need the right pack by Friday for a clinic. Can your team arrange an immediate replacement? Katarina" Reply to Katarina, a peer, and apologise for the error.
tasks: Apologise for the wrong pack size and confirm you understand the Friday deadline.
Say what you will do now: check stock of 60 millilitre packs and arrange express shipping.
Explain how the customer should return the wrong bottles and promise an update by tomorrow.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Your team is moving a respiratory product family to a regional planning team in the UK, and your peer Carlos will take it over on 1 July. You want to arrange a smooth handover and find out what he needs. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Carlos that the respiratory product family moves to his team on 1 July.
Ask what information he needs, such as forecast files, supplier contacts and open orders.
Suggest a first handover call next week and offer two possible time slots.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company, and a product family is moving from your team to a regional team in Spain. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, I will take over the cold-chain biologic family from 1 December. Could you send me the current forecast file and tell me which shipments are still open? I would also like the name of the freight forwarder contact. Can we hold a handover call before 20 November? Kind regards, Mark Brandt" Reply to Mark and answer each point. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Mark and confirm the 1 December takeover of the cold-chain biologic family.
Answer his questions about the forecast file, the open shipments and the freight forwarder contact.
Propose a specific date and time for the handover call before 20 November.

situation: You are a demand planner, and from January every planning report must follow a new naming convention that includes region, product code and cycle month. Priya, a peer in Sweden, still sends clinical-supply kit reports with the old names, and the first audit is on 8 December. You need her to switch and to tell you if she needs help. Be polite but make the urgency clear.
tasks: Explain that the new naming convention becomes mandatory in January and mention the 8 December audit.
Ask Priya to rename her clinical-supply kit reports and send you one example for checking.
Offer a short call or a template to help her, and ask for a reply by Friday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning from a colleague in another region. "Hi, I read your business case for the three-month data-quality clean-up. I like it, but my director asks what it costs in working hours and what we gain on the oral solid dose tablet forecast. Can you also tell me when it could start? Thanks, Samir" Reply to Samir with clear answers to both questions. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Thank Samir and say you are glad the director is reviewing the clean-up business case.
Answer his question about working hours, and describe the expected gain in tablet forecast accuracy.
Give a possible start date and ask him to confirm what the director needs next.

situation: A graduate from your regional team in Mexico will rotate through the planning group for six months, and Mark Costa coordinates the programme. The graduate needs a first project that is useful but safe, ideally about a device sub-assembly with a clear end date. You want his view on scope before the rotation begins in January. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Introduce yourself and say why you are writing about the graduate rotation starting in January.
Propose a first project, such as reviewing lead times for the device sub-assembly, with a clear deliverable.
Ask Mark to confirm the scope and to name a mentor for the first month.

situation: A supplier changed a raw-material specification for your clinical-supply kits without telling you, and the change was found during incoming inspection on Tuesday. Your manager Andre in Japan is worried about trial deadlines. No kits have shipped with the new material, and the supplier has promised a full report. Reassure him in your update.
tasks: State what happened: the supplier changed the specification without notice and the inspection found it on Tuesday.
Explain that no affected kits have shipped and that the trial timelines are protected for now.
Say what you will do next, including the supplier report and a follow-up on Friday.

situation:
You will be on leave for two weeks from 3 November, and Marta Lindqvist, a colleague in Mexico, will cover your paediatric suspension products. After a short handover with your manager you kept these notes:
- cover period 3 to 14 Nov, Marta owns all orders
- weekly forecast upload due Monday 9 Nov
- one open deviation on batch PS-114, QA contact Lena
- do not release the Mexico order above 4,000 units without approval
- I am reachable only for emergencies by phone
Write the follow-up email to your manager. Stay friendly.
tasks: Summarise the cover arrangement and confirm that Marta handles your paediatric suspension products during the leave.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the Monday forecast upload and the open deviation.
Flag the approval limit on the Mexico order and ask your manager to confirm the emergency contact rule.

situation: OTIF for one customer in Chile fell to 82 percent last month, and the account manager is upset. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, the customer called me twice about late biologic deliveries. They say two shipments arrived four days late. Can you tell me what happened and when they will be back on target? I need something to tell them today. Thanks, Nadia" Reply to Nadia with an honest explanation and a recovery date. Stay friendly.
tasks: Acknowledge Nadia's concern and apologise for the two shipments that arrived four days late.
Explain the main causes of the OTIF drop to 82 percent in simple terms.
Give a realistic recovery date and say what Nadia can tell the customer today.

situation: Peak season starts in six weeks and your team of three planners already works long hours. Your manager Andre Petrov has not yet approved extra budget for a temporary planner for the device sub-assembly portfolio in Mexico, even though you sent the request in September. You need an answer this week. Describe the problem and state what you want clearly. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Remind Andre that the September request for a temporary planner is still waiting for a decision.
Describe the risk to the device sub-assembly forecasts if the team stays at three planners during peak.
Ask for a decision by Friday and suggest a three-month contract as a solution.

situation: A supplier contact in Ireland has sent you this message. "Hello, from Monday the approval workflow for expedited shipments changes. Every rush order will need two sign-offs, yours and one from finance, before we release the truck. For the cardiovascular tablets, we need the new form by 10:00 on the order day. Is this workable for you? Best, Daniel" Reply to Daniel, confirm what works, and raise one practical concern. Stay friendly.
tasks: Thank Daniel for the notice and confirm you understand the two sign-offs required from Monday.
Raise a concern about the 10:00 deadline for cardiovascular tablet orders and suggest an alternative time.
Ask Daniel for the new form and a contact for urgent questions.

situation: Your manager Yuki sent you this message about the forecasting tool. "Hi, the licence for our forecasting tool ends on 31 January. Finance will only renew if we show the value. Could you send me a short justification for one more year, with the cost and the benefit for the oncology infusion portfolio? I need it by next Wednesday. Thanks, Yuki" Reply with a clear summary of what you will send and when. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Confirm that you will prepare the justification for the licence extension before next Wednesday.
Outline the benefit for the oncology infusion portfolio, such as fewer manual corrections and better accuracy.
Ask Yuki for the current licence cost and the finance template, if there is one.

situation: A pallet of active ingredient shipped from your supplier in Poland recorded a temperature excursion of 11 degrees for about three hours in transit. The pallet is quarantined at your warehouse and QA is reviewing the data logger file. You must tell Nadia Fischer at the supplier what you found and what you need from her. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Describe the excursion on the pallet, including the temperature reached and its approximate duration.
State that the pallet is quarantined and that QA is reviewing the data logger file.
Request the supplier's transport records and a stability statement by Thursday.

situation: Your carrier cannot deliver the diabetes product order to your Irish site on Friday because the receiving dock is closed for maintenance. You want to move the delivery to Monday morning. Katarina Tanaka at the supplier is worried about disruption, and stock cover is still comfortable. Reassure her in your update.
tasks: Explain that the dock is closed on Friday and that you want to move the delivery to Monday.
Reassure Katarina that stock cover is sufficient and that this change causes no shortage.
Ask her to confirm the Monday slot and to update the booking with the carrier.

situation: A shipment of vial-based injectables stopped at customs late last night and the issue is still open. Your shift ends now, and Elena works in Brazil, several hours behind you. She will continue the case when she starts, so she needs facts, not a story. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Summarise the shipment issue: what stopped at customs, when, and the current status.
List what you already did, including who you contacted and which documents are missing.
Say what Elena should do first on her shift and where to find the case file.

situation:
You held a call with Rahul Walsh, a customer in Egypt, about an invoice that does not match the delivered quantity of a diabetes product. Your notes:
- invoice shows 12,000 pens, delivery note shows 10,800
- customer received 10,800, confirmed by warehouse count
- 1,200 pens still in our dock, error in order system
- credit note to be issued by finance, owner Leila, by 20 Nov
- Rahul to confirm in writing if the missing pens are still needed
Write the follow-up email to Rahul. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Summarise the discrepancy between the invoice and the delivery note and what was agreed on the call.
List the actions, including the credit note owner and the 20 November date.
Ask Rahul to confirm in writing whether he still needs the 1,200 missing pens.

situation: A secondary packaging component will run out in South Africa in about three weeks, and an air-freight transfer from another site could close the gap. It costs roughly five times the sea freight, so you need Viktor Ahmed, who manages the budget for that region, to agree to share the cost. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain the stock-out risk for the packaging component and the date when stock runs out.
Describe the air-freight option and its cost, and ask Viktor to approve a shared budget.
Request an answer by Wednesday so that the transfer can leave on Thursday.

situation: A new peer in Spain called Kenji will shadow your planning cycle for one week, starting Monday 16 November. He has to see the respiratory product forecast review on Tuesday, but you have not agreed the schedule yet. You need a reply today so you can book the rooms. Be polite and show the urgency.
tasks: Welcome Kenji and say that you are writing to agree the schedule for his week of shadowing.
Ask which meetings he most wants to see, especially the Tuesday respiratory forecast review.
Request his availability and any system access he needs by the end of today.

situation: The consignee for your biologic shipments in India moved to a new warehouse, so the shipping address changed on 1 November. Several open orders still point to the old address, and two pallets are due next week. Ingrid, a peer in the logistics team, can correct the orders in the system. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Ingrid that the shipping address in India changed on 1 November.
Explain that some open orders still use the old address and mention the two pallets due next week.
Ask her to update the orders and confirm when the corrections are done.

situation: You planned a three-hour kick-off meeting with a customer, Peter Walsh, in Australia for a vial-based injectable programme. Because of the time difference, three hours is too long for both teams. You want to split it into two shorter sessions of ninety minutes on consecutive days. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain that you want to split the kick-off meeting into two ninety-minute sessions.
Propose two slots that suit the Australian time zone, one on Tuesday and one on Wednesday.
Ask Peter to confirm and to send any agenda points he wants to add.

situation: Your company introduces a standard template for demand-review notes in all regions. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, from next month every region has to use the new template for demand-review notes. It has five sections and must be uploaded within two days of the meeting. Can your Mexico team confirm that it works for you? Also tell me if any section is unclear. Regards, Mei Ruiz" Answer Mei. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Confirm that your team can use the new demand-review template from next month.
Respond to the two-day upload rule and say whether it is realistic.
Mention one section that needs clarification and ask Mei for an example.

situation: Your paediatric suspension family is moving to a regional team in India, but the handover started only a week before the transfer date and several documents are missing. Hannah, the regional lead, has not answered your questions about open orders. You are disappointed and want a proper handover plan. Stay professional.
tasks: State that the transfer date is close and that the handover documents are still incomplete.
Say you are disappointed that your earlier questions about open orders have not been answered.
Ask Hannah for a handover plan with named owners by next Monday.

situation: Until now the central team ran the supplier-forecast process, but from January the regional team in Turkey takes it over. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I need to know who from your side will train the regional planners and how long it should take. Also, do you want to keep a monthly check for the first quarter? Best, Kenji Hall" Reply to your manager Kenji with a clear proposal. Stay friendly.
tasks: Say who will train the regional planners and give an estimate of the training time.
Respond to his question and recommend a monthly check during the first quarter.
Offer to prepare a training outline by the end of next week.

situation: A competitor launched a rival device last month, and you expect demand for your mature device sub-assembly to fall by about 15 percent next year. Your manager Lucas in Egypt may worry about the plan and the inventory already ordered. Explain what changes in the forecast and what you will do about it. Be reassuring.
tasks: Explain that the competitor's launch lowers the sub-assembly forecast by about 15 percent.
Show how you will adjust open orders and inventory to avoid excess stock.
Say when you will share the revised numbers and offer to discuss them this week.

situation: A new analyst called Mei Larsen joins your team in Singapore, and she must learn the main planning systems before the month-end close on 30 November. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, I start Monday. Which systems should I learn first? Is there any training I should book before the close? Thanks, Mei" Reply as her manager colleague with a short learning plan. Stay friendly.
tasks: Welcome Mei and name the first two systems she should learn before the close.
Suggest a weekly learning plan and mention any training worth booking.
Offer a short meeting on Monday and ask her to tell you if access is missing.

situation: A new team lead called Amira joined the Turkey team and asked for the planning calendar, but the calendar she received omits the S&OP cut-off dates, and last week this caused a late submission. You work in another region and need the calendar to be accurate. Raise the issue and ask for a corrected version. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the calendar sent to Amira omits the S&OP cut-off dates.
Describe how the missing dates caused a late submission last week.
Ask her to send a corrected calendar by Friday and to name an owner.

situation: Two regions are competing for the same limited batch of prefilled pens. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear colleague, we need the whole batch of 6,000 pens for our tender in Chile. Delay would cost us the contract. Please release it by Friday. Daniel Novak" You cannot give everything, because another region has urgent patient orders. Reply to Daniel, offer a split, and hold your position. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Acknowledge the tender deadline and the risk of losing the Chile contract.
Explain that you cannot release all 6,000 pens because another region has urgent patient orders.
Propose a split of the batch and ask Daniel to confirm by Thursday.

situation: A pilot of automatic safety-stock recalculation starts in Canada and one other country. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, we are still waiting for your list of prefilled pen items for the pilot. It was due on Monday. Can you send it today and tell me why it was late? Marta" You missed the date because of a system issue. Reply to your manager and apologise. Be apologetic.
tasks: Apologise for sending the prefilled pen list after the Monday deadline.
Explain briefly that a system issue caused the delay, without blaming anyone.
Attach the list, or promise it today, and suggest how to avoid another delay.

situation: The owner of a safety-stock review, a colleague called Katarina Nair, is changing role next week, and her notes about clinical-supply kits are scattered across email and folders in Brazil. You are writing to her to say that you will collect everything into one document. Ask her for what is missing. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Inform Katarina that you are gathering her safety-stock review notes into one document.
List what is still missing, such as assumptions, service levels and the last approval.
Ask her to review the document before she leaves and to name a back-up contact.

situation: During the pandemic customers in Chile bought device sub-assemblies in large quantities, but this stockpiling has disappeared and the baseline in the forecast is too high. You have found that the last 18 months distort the statistical model. Daniel Ruiz, a peer, uses the same data. Tell him what you will reset and when. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that the stockpiling pattern has ended and that the current baseline is too high.
Say which months you will exclude from the statistical model and why.
Tell Daniel when the new baseline will be ready and ask for his comments.

situation: Your supplier in Egypt delivered only half of the ordered glass vials for an oncology infusion, 20,000 out of 40,000, and gave no date for the rest. The line needs the vials in ten days. You are writing to Rahul Hall to ask for a firm delivery plan. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State the order quantity, the quantity received and the missing amount of glass vials.
Explain that the oncology line needs the rest within ten days.
Ask Rahul for a confirmed delivery date and for the cause of the shortage.

situation: A logistics provider in Germany announced a 6 percent rate increase from February. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello, finance wants to know what we will answer to the carrier before the end of the month. Do you have a counter-offer? I also need the volume numbers. Thanks, Daniel Moreau" You promised the paediatric suspension volumes last week but forgot. Reply, apologise and propose a counter-offer.
tasks: Apologise for not sending the paediatric suspension volume numbers last week.
Attach the volumes, or say exactly when you will send them.
Propose a counter-offer, such as a smaller increase tied to a yearly volume commitment.

situation: A new rule requires a second check before any manual forecast override, and your team in the UK now loses a full day each cycle waiting for it. Tom Moreau, who owns the process in another region, did not consult your team. You are disappointed but want to find a practical solution. Stay professional.
tasks: Say that the second check before a manual override delays your prefilled pen forecast by about a day.
Point out that your team was not consulted before the rule started.
Suggest a threshold below which overrides need no second check and ask Tom for a call.

situation: Safety stock for a cold-chain biologic in Mexico was consumed by an unplanned export order that nobody discussed with you, and the stock now covers only nine days. Tom, who manages the other region, approved it on his own. You need to protect patient supply. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that the export order used the safety stock of the cold-chain biologic in Mexico.
Explain the consequence: only nine days of cover remain and supply to patients is at risk.
Ask Tom to agree to a rule that exports above a set size need prior discussion.

situation: A data logger failed during a shipment of vial-based injectables to Turkey, so no temperature record exists for the transit. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi, QA says we cannot release the shipment without data. Do we know where it is now? And what do you recommend? Please answer today. Viktor Reyes" Reply to your manager and recommend a course of action. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Tell Viktor where the shipment is now and when it arrived at the warehouse.
Explain that without data from the logger the shipment must stay in quarantine.
Recommend a next step, such as asking QA for a stability assessment, and offer to coordinate.

situation:
You met Peter Larsen, a new team lead in Chile, to walk through the planning calendar of your diabetes product portfolio. Your notes:
- demand review on the second Tuesday of each month
- supply review on the following Thursday
- S&OP pre-meeting on day 15, final on day 20
- Peter joins the supply review as observer first
- calendar file to be shared by Monday, owner me
- Peter to list open questions about cut-off times
Write the follow-up email to Peter. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Summarise the planning calendar you explained, naming each review and its timing.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the calendar file due on Monday.
Ask Peter to send his open questions about cut-off times and confirm his observer role.

situation: The owner of a weekly inventory report has left the company and you inherit it from this Monday. The report goes to peers in several sites, including Oliver in the UK, who uses it for respiratory product decisions. You will keep the format for four weeks and then discuss improvements. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Tell Oliver that you now own the weekly inventory report, starting from Monday.
Explain that the format stays the same for four weeks to avoid confusion.
Ask him which figures he uses most and invite his suggestions for later.

situation: A batch of vial-based injectables is on hold because of a documentation gap in the deviation investigation, and Ben, who works in the Australia region, wrote to you. "Hello, my customer orders are waiting for that batch. Can you tell me when it will be released and whether there is an alternative? I have to answer the account manager today. Ben" Reply with the status, an estimate and options. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the batch is on hold while the documentation gap in the investigation is resolved.
Give your best estimate of the release date and say what it depends on.
Offer options for Ben's customer orders, such as another batch or a partial shipment.

situation: Your flight to a regional planning workshop in the UK was cancelled, and the next available flight arrives after the first session ends. Mei, a peer who organises the workshop, needs to know whether you can attend. You have a few options, including joining the first morning by video. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Mei that your flight to the workshop was cancelled and explain the new arrival time.
Offer to join the first morning remotely and ask whether this is possible.
Say you will confirm your plans by tomorrow noon and ask who can cover the paediatric suspension agenda item.

situation: Your carrier moved a delivery of cold-chain biologic from Friday to Monday because the receiving dock in Turkey is closed, but nobody warned you, and a product that must stay cold waited over the weekend in a transit hub. You are writing to Hannah Moreau, who coordinates the dock. Raise the issue and ask for a fix. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that the delivery moved from Friday to Monday without notice because the receiving dock was closed.
Explain the risk for the cold-chain biologic during the weekend wait.
Ask Hannah to share dock closure dates in advance and confirm a contact for changes.

situation: The cleaning verification record for an oncology infusion line in Brazil was incomplete, so the line must be re-checked before the next batch. This delays your plan by two days. Kenji, from the other region, owns the line documentation. You are disappointed but professional, and you want the record completed. Stay professional.
tasks: Explain that the cleaning verification record for the oncology infusion line is incomplete.
Describe the two-day delay to your production plan caused by the re-check.
Ask Kenji to complete the record and to confirm a new date for the line.

situation: An intern called Sofia will join your planning team in Italy for three months from 2 February. Your manager Carlos Rossi asked how you plan to use her time on the inhaler portfolio. You have a desk, system access and a first small project in mind. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Confirm that the intern starts on 2 February and that her desk and access are being arranged.
Describe the first project, such as cleaning the inhaler demand history, and the expected result.
Say who will supervise her each week and when you will review her progress.

situation: Projected inventory for an oncology infusion at your customer in Spain turns negative in about six weeks if nothing changes. The customer contact, Oliver Ahmed, has not planned for this. You want to warn him early and suggest ways to avoid a stock-out, such as a split delivery. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Oliver that projected inventory of the oncology infusion turns negative in about six weeks.
Explain the main cause and what happens if nothing changes.
Suggest a split delivery and propose a call this week to agree the plan.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Marta Petrov buys a respiratory product for a pharmacy chain in Sweden. On Tuesday an unplanned export order used up the safety stock for that item, and the next batch is released only in twelve days. You want to update her on the situation and on what you are doing about it. Be calm and reassuring.
tasks: Explain briefly that an unplanned export order used the safety stock for her respiratory product.
State the weekly volume you can still guarantee until the new batch is released.
Describe the recovery steps and promise a written update on a specific day.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Tom plans supply in Ireland and holds a small buffer of an active ingredient that your site also uses. An unplanned export order has consumed your own safety stock, and your next internal delivery is not due until the end of the month. You need him to release part of his buffer this week. Sound polite but make the urgency clear.
tasks: Open by explaining that an export order consumed your safety stock of the active ingredient.
Ask Tom to release a specific quantity from his buffer before Friday.
Offer to replace the quantity from your next delivery and ask for a reply today.

situation: A tender win in Germany will raise next quarter's demand for a cardiovascular tablet by 25 percent. Carlos Fischer plans for the regional distribution centre in another region and has not yet seen the new number. You need his confirmation that his side can absorb the extra volume and that he will update his own forecast. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Introduce the tender win and say it raises next quarter's tablet demand by 25 percent.
Ask Carlos whether the distribution centre can handle the higher monthly volume from July.
Request his updated forecast by next Wednesday and offer a short call to align.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, I heard you spoke with the contract manufacturer about our paediatric suspension. Procurement needs to know whether we can still revise the Spanish forecast without paying a penalty, and until which date. We plan to present the new numbers on 14 March. Kind regards, Julia Silva" You negotiated a penalty-free revision window last week, and you must now reply to Julia. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Confirm that you negotiated a penalty-free window for revising the Spanish suspension forecast.
State the exact closing date and the maximum size of change the manufacturer accepts.
Explain what you need from Julia before her 14 March presentation and thank her.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A regulatory approval in a new market has produced a demand spike for a prefilled pen that no history can explain. Katarina Walsh, who runs commercial planning in Ireland, knew about the approval date but did not share it with you. Your forecast missed the spike by a wide margin. You need her to explain the plan and to share launch information earlier in future. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Describe the demand spike for the prefilled pen and say your forecast did not anticipate it.
Point out that the approval date was not shared with planning in time.
Ask Katarina to send launch volumes and dates and to agree a regular update.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Your manager Ben Brandt in the UK has asked how open shipment issues for clinical-supply kits are tracked. Last month you replaced long email chains with a shared tracker that logs each issue, its owner and its due date. You want to report the first results and what happens next. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Announce that a shared tracker now replaces email chains for open clinical-supply kit shipment issues.
Report the first results, such as the number of issues closed and their average age.
Explain next steps and ask Ben whether to extend the tracker to other product lines.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Mark Nair, a new peer from Japan, is shadowing your planning cycle for a week. He has joined meetings but has not read the prefilled pen planning notes you sent, and on Wednesday he asked you to repeat the full background twice. You want him to prepare so the week is useful for both of you. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Say that you are happy to host Mark but need him to prepare before each session.
Point out that the prefilled pen notes were sent on Monday and ask him to read them.
Propose a fixed daily fifteen-minute slot for questions and ask him to confirm it.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, thanks for the handover file. I opened it yesterday and I cannot find the supplier confirmations for three of the injectable purchase orders, and two delivery dates look wrong. I start covering your desk on Monday, so I would like to sort this out before then. Katarina" You are going on parental leave, and you must reply and apologise for the gaps in your handover.
tasks: Apologise for the missing supplier confirmations and the two wrong delivery dates in the handover file.
Explain where the three confirmations are stored and correct the dates you know.
Offer a thirty-minute call before Monday and promise an updated file by Friday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, I received your half-finished forecast analysis for the tablet after the reorganisation, but I cannot tell which assumptions are final. The 2027 volumes also seem to stop at August. Could you explain what is still open and when I can expect the rest? Thanks, Hannah Rossi" The analysis was handed over before it was ready, and you must reply to Hannah.
tasks: Apologise for sending the analysis unfinished and for the confusion about which assumptions are final.
List the assumptions that are still open and explain why the 2027 volumes stop at August.
Promise a completed version by a specific date and offer a call to go through it.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A rounding error in the planning tool understated demand for an oncology infusion over a three-month horizon in India. Daniel, who owns the tool configuration in another region, was told about the issue in September but nothing changed. You now risk a shortfall of several hundred units. Explain this to him and ask for a fix. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Describe how the rounding error understated three months of infusion demand and put supply at risk.
Remind Daniel that the problem was first reported in September and is still unresolved.
Ask for a corrected configuration within one week and a date for the next check.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. For more than a year you and your manager Ben Fischer have met every Monday at nine. Since the inhaler launch in Ireland you have a recurring supplier call at that time, so the slot no longer works. You want to propose a new rhythm for your one-to-ones. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that your Monday slot now clashes with a recurring inhaler supplier call.
Propose a fortnightly forty-five minute meeting on Thursday mornings with a short written update in between.
Ask Ben to confirm the new rhythm and say you will send the updated invitation.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. On-time-in-full delivery of an oncology infusion to one German customer fell to 82 percent last month, and the account manager has complained to your manager Carlos Walsh. He has asked you for a clear picture. You know two late batch releases and one carrier delay caused most of the gap. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that on-time-in-full delivery to the German customer fell to 82 percent last month.
Explain the two late batch releases and the carrier delay behind the drop.
Describe the corrective actions and the date by which you expect to reach 95 percent.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Your invitation to a review of respiratory product supply in Egypt went to the wrong distribution list, so several key people never received it. Peter Reyes is a customer contact who should have joined, and the meeting is next Tuesday at ten. You want to fix the mistake and get him and his colleagues there. Stay friendly.
tasks: Apologise for sending the invitation to the wrong distribution list.
Ask Peter to forward the new invitation to the colleagues who should attend the Tuesday review.
Explain the agenda in one sentence and offer to move the time if needed.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Viktor has just joined a peer team in Turkey as its new lead and wants to understand how the planning calendar works for prefilled pens. You can explain the monthly cycle: demand review in week one, supply review in week two, and the S&OP meeting in week three. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Welcome Viktor and say you will explain the monthly planning calendar for prefilled pens.
Summarise the cycle: demand review, supply review and the S&OP meeting, with the week of each.
Offer a walkthrough session and attach the calendar for him to check.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I saw that the safety stock for the clinical kits is gone. Can you tell me what happened and whether next week's orders in the UK are still covered? I need to answer the sponsor team by Thursday. Thanks, Sofia Ruiz" An unplanned export order used the safety stock. Reply to your manager.
tasks: Explain that an unplanned export order consumed the safety stock for the clinical kits.
Confirm whether next week's UK orders are covered and give the quantities.
State what you will do before her Thursday deadline to rebuild the buffer.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. From next month your team starts a weekly exception-based planning routine, where planners only review items that breach agreed thresholds. Nadia Walsh works on respiratory products in Ireland and needs to know what to prepare. You want to explain the routine and ask her to nominate one person for the first session. Stay friendly.
tasks: Introduce the new weekly exception-based routine that starts next month.
Explain in one or two sentences which thresholds trigger a review for respiratory items.
Ask Nadia to nominate a participant by Friday and offer a short briefing.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, I return on Monday after six months of leave. I understand the planning process changed while I was away, and I would like to know what is different before my first meeting with the Mexico team. Best regards, Andre" Several things changed for the device sub-assembly, and you must reply to him. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Welcome Andre back and say you will summarise what changed while he was away.
Describe the two or three main process changes that affect the device sub-assembly.
Suggest a meeting before his first Mexico team session and mention a document for him.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A quality deviation on a diabetes product closed three days late, and the planned release date now sits at risk. Fatima manages distribution in Italy and has orders waiting for this batch. You need to tell her what happened, the new earliest release date, and what she should plan for. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that the deviation closed three days late and the release date is at risk.
Give the new earliest release date and the confidence you have in it.
Say what Fatima should plan for in Italy and when you will send the next update.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. From next month the end-of-month inventory reconciliation has a stricter cut-off: Friday at noon instead of Monday. Viktor Novak, a peer in Australia, usually sends his active ingredient counts on Monday afternoon, so your reports will be late. You want him to adapt his timing. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Explain that the reconciliation cut-off for the active ingredient counts moves to Friday at noon.
Say that Monday submissions from Australia will delay your consolidated report.
Ask Viktor to confirm he can deliver counts by the new deadline and suggest a trial.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Mark Walsh has just joined a peer team in Germany as team lead and has asked about planning dates. You need a copy of the team's active ingredient planning calendar so you can align your own supply reviews with his. You also want a short introductory call. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Introduce yourself and say you work on active ingredient supply planning.
Ask Mark to send his team's planning calendar for the active ingredient with the key review dates.
Propose a short introductory call next week and offer your own calendar in return.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, the carrier can deliver your cardiovascular tablets to Istanbul on Friday as planned, but I understand the receiving dock is closed that day. Please confirm whether we should hold the truck or reschedule. We need an answer by noon. Regards, Daniel" Reply and move the delivery to Monday.
tasks: Confirm that the delivery moves from Friday to Monday because the receiving dock is closed.
Ask Daniel to rebook the truck and state the time window the dock accepts on Monday.
Request written confirmation before noon and a note of any extra storage charge.

situation:
You chaired a monthly forecast review with a key customer contact in Spain, Viktor Moreau, about secondary packaging components. Forecast accuracy fell below target last month because of one large unexpected order. Your notes:
- Accuracy 71 percent against 85 percent target
- One 40,000-unit order placed without notice
- Customer to share order pipeline weekly, owner Viktor
- Planning adds order alert to forecast model, you, by 22 May
- Next review 4 June; revisit the safety stock level
Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Summarise the main outcome: accuracy fell to 71 percent because of one unexpected 40,000-unit order.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the weekly pipeline and the order alert.
Ask Viktor to confirm the actions and flag the safety stock level as an open point.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, our project is ending on 30 November and I understand your team will take over run-state support. Could you confirm that the handover documents will be complete by then? Our operations team in Australia cannot start without them. Hannah Rossi" You must reply and confirm what is ready for the oncology infusion. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Confirm that run-state support for the oncology infusion transfers on 30 November as planned.
State which handover documents are complete and which will follow, with dates.
Say clearly that the date cannot move and ask Hannah to confirm her team's readiness.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Until now a central team ran the supply planning process for oral solid dose tablets, and from January the regional team in Chile takes it over. Your manager Hannah Fischer has asked how the transition is going. Training finished last week and the first cycle runs in January. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Hannah that the Chile regional team will take over the tablet planning process in January.
Report that training finished last week and mention one remaining risk.
Explain the next steps, including the first joint cycle and when you will report again.

situation:
You chaired a short supply call with Julia Ruiz and her team in Mexico after a carrier strike in Europe delayed inbound active ingredient for a vial-based injectable by about a week. Your notes:
- Strike began Monday; two pallets stuck in Rotterdam
- Delay about seven days; no output loss in November
- Air freight of one pallet agreed, owner Julia, booking by Thursday
- Safety stock cover drops to nine days
- You update the forecast and share the new plan by Friday
- Next call Tuesday 9:00 Mexico time
Stay friendly.
tasks: Summarise the situation and the decisions: seven-day delay, no November output loss, one pallet by air.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the Thursday booking and your Friday plan.
Ask Julia to confirm the notes and flag the nine-day safety stock cover as an open point.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A market in India could run out of a key strength of a prefilled pen about nine days before the next shipment lands. Your manager needs to know before the weekly meeting. You have checked stock and confirmed an air-freight option for part of the volume. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State that the Indian market could run out of the key pen strength before the shipment arrives.
Give the stock-out date, the size of the gap and the root cause.
Propose the air-freight option for part of the volume and ask for approval today.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, thank you for your request to visit the packaging supplier in Japan for the quality audit. Before I can approve the travel budget I need a cost breakdown and a short explanation of why a remote audit is not enough. Please send both by Friday. Kind regards, Nadia Walsh" Reply to Nadia. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Thank Nadia and say you will provide the cost breakdown for the trip to Japan.
Explain why a remote audit cannot replace an on-site check of the packaging line.
Give the proposed travel dates, the total estimate and the date by which you need approval.

situation:
You organised a supplier meeting with Chloe Costa about delivery plans for an inhaler, but the invitation went to the wrong distribution list and two key people missed it. You have now caught up with Chloe separately. Your notes:
- Invitation reached the old list; two planners absent
- Chloe confirmed capacity for 60,000 units in Q1
- Lead time stays at eight weeks
- You re-send the invitation list, by Monday
- Chloe sends capacity table in writing, by Wednesday
- Full group meeting moved to 18 February
Stay friendly.
tasks: Apologise briefly for the wrong distribution list and summarise what you agreed with Chloe.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the capacity table and the new invitation.
Ask Chloe to confirm the 18 February meeting and flag the eight-week lead time as open.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hello Alex, a hospital pharmacy in Cork says deliveries of the paediatric suspension keep arriving after the agreed morning window, three times this month. They want an explanation and a fix this week. Can you tell me what is going on? Fatima" Fatima works in another region. Reply with the cause you found and the next step.
tasks: Acknowledge the three late deliveries to the Cork hospital pharmacy this month.
Explain the cause you found, such as a changed carrier route or late release.
Propose a concrete fix, who owns it and the date by which the window will be met.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. You go on leave next week and your colleague will cover your open purchase orders for a diabetes product. Samir, your manager in Turkey, needs to approve the cover arrangement and give your colleague access to the ordering system. There are still four orders to confirm. Sound polite but urgent.
tasks: State that you go on leave next week and need cover for the open purchase orders.
Ask Samir to approve system access for your colleague by Wednesday.
Mention the four unconfirmed orders and offer to prepare a handover list.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I hear the new sub-supplier for our tablet is still in qualification. Is it true that deliveries move by three weeks? The Spanish launch is planned for 15 November and I need to tell the commercial team today. Thanks, Nadia" The qualification is slower than promised. Reply to her.
tasks: Confirm that the sub-supplier qualification is slower than promised and deliveries move by three weeks.
Say whether the 15 November launch in Spain is affected and offer a partial option.
Promise to send the revised plan and a decision date by tomorrow.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Amira Fischer plans production at a peer site in Japan. A supplier delay on an inhaler component will not hurt this month's output, but it eats all the safety stock for next month. You need her to move up a planned component order of about 20,000 units. Sound polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that the supplier delay will not affect this month's output but empties next month's safety stock.
Ask Amira to bring forward the planned component order of 20,000 units.
Request her answer by tomorrow and say what you will do if she cannot.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, our raw material for your oncology infusion will leave eleven days late because of a quality hold at our site. I assume this does not affect your output this month. Please confirm and tell us if you need anything else. Regards, Ben Fischer" The output is fine, but the delay uses all next month's safety stock. Reply to the supplier.
tasks: Confirm that this month's infusion output is not affected by the eleven-day delay.
Explain that the delay uses up all of next month's safety stock.
Ask the supplier for a split shipment and a revised dispatch date by Friday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A tender win will raise next quarter's demand for a cardiovascular tablet by 25 percent, but your manager Viktor in Poland did not tell planning until the contract was signed. You now have little time to secure materials. You want to raise this with him and ask for earlier information. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that the tender win raises next quarter's tablet demand by 25 percent and planning learned late.
Explain what the short notice means for material orders and lead times.
Ask Viktor to involve planning before tender submission and propose a standing check-in.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the printed packaging for the prefilled pen reached us two days after the filling slot, so the line sat idle on Tuesday. This costs us a lot. Can you explain what happened and how to avoid it? Rahul Haddad" The artwork approval from your side was late. Apologise and reply.
tasks: Apologise for the late artwork approval that delayed the packaging and left the line idle.
Explain what caused the delay on your side in one or two sentences.
Propose a new filling slot and a rule to approve artwork a week earlier.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Yuki is your contact at a vial supplier in the UK. You expect to raise your annual volume by about a third next year, and you want payment terms of sixty days instead of thirty in return. You have a good relationship and want to open the conversation before the contract review. Stay friendly.
tasks: Share your expected annual volume increase for the vial-based injectable next year.
Propose sixty-day payment terms in exchange for the larger commitment.
Suggest a call before the contract review and ask Yuki to send his view.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A key account in Singapore demands a recovery plan after a stock-out of a device sub-assembly. Elena Lindqvist leads purchasing there and wants to know when supply returns to normal. You have a plan with weekly partial shipments but need her to confirm priorities. Sound polite but urgent.
tasks: Acknowledge the stock-out of the device sub-assembly and the impact on her operations.
Present the recovery plan with weekly partial shipments and the date supply normalises.
Ask Elena to confirm the priority order of her sites by Thursday.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A new rule in your planning group requires a second check before any manual forecast override. Tom, a peer in Spain, often overrides diabetes product numbers late on Fridays. You want him to know how the rule works and to act as your reviewer for a month. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain the new rule requiring a second check before any manual forecast override.
Ask Tom to review your overrides for the diabetes product during the next month.
Offer to check his overrides in return and suggest a simple way to log them.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A cold-chain data logger failed during a biologic shipment to India, so you cannot prove the vials stayed within temperature. Nadia Petrov manages the shipping partner in another region and the batch is on hold. You want her to investigate and tell you how to prevent a repeat. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Report that the data logger failed during the biologic shipment and the batch is on hold.
Ask Nadia to get the logger data and a written explanation within three working days.
Request a plan to prevent repeats, including backup loggers on future shipments.
