situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. A hospital customer reports that its remaining stock of an oral tablet lasts about ten days. Tom handles distribution for the Swedish market as a peer, and you need to know if he holds any free stock that can be released. You also want a delivery date. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: State that a hospital customer in Sweden has only ten days of tablet stock left.
Ask Tom how many tablets he can release from free stock and when.
Request a confirmed delivery date by tomorrow so you can inform the hospital.

situation: You are a demand planner at a pharmaceutical company. Peter Petrov is a contact at a supplier in Sweden. From next month purchase order confirmations for the device sub-assembly will be tracked in a new tool instead of spreadsheets. He must register and confirm each order there within two working days. You need him to set up access quickly. Sound polite but urgent.
tasks: Explain that a new tool replaces spreadsheets for tracking purchase order confirmations for the sub-assembly.
Ask Peter to register two users and confirm their names by next Wednesday.
Say that confirmations should happen within two working days and offer a training session.

situation: You are a demand planner and you were due to fly to Istanbul for a regional workshop on respiratory product forecasts. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the airline cancelled Tuesday's evening flight to Istanbul. Are you still able to join the workshop on Wednesday at 9:00? I need to confirm the room and the catering by Monday noon. If you cannot make it, could you present your slides by video link? Thanks, Laura Tanaka" You write back to Laura, a colleague in another region, to say what you can and cannot do. Keep the tone neutral and factual.
tasks: Thank Laura and confirm you received her note about the cancelled Tuesday evening flight.
Say whether you can still reach Istanbul for Wednesday at 9:00 and what you are doing to rebook.
Offer the video-link option as a backup and promise a final answer before Monday noon.

situation: You are a planner at a pharma plant in Germany. The site moved its goods-in dock to a new street address on 1 March, but Mei Larsen's company is still sending open orders for secondary packaging components to the old one. Two pallets of cartons were redirected last week and a third is due Thursday. Write to Mei and ask her to fix the address in every open order. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that your receiving address changed on 1 March and that open orders still show the old one.
Describe the impact, including the two redirected pallets and the one due on Thursday.
Ask Mei to update all open orders and confirm in writing by Wednesday.

situation: You are a supply planner for a diabetes product sold in Japan. The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, from 1 December procurement will own the relationship with our insulin pen needle supplier, so planning steps back. Could you write a short handover note with the open purchase orders and the known quality issues? Also please join the call with the supplier on Thursday at 14:00 so they hear it from both of us. Thanks, Sofia" Reply to Sofia, your manager, and agree to the handover. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Confirm you understand the change of ownership from planning to procurement on 1 December.
Promise the handover note with open purchase orders and known quality issues and give a delivery date.
Accept the Thursday 14:00 supplier call and ask what Sofia wants you to say there.

situation: A revised approval workflow for expedited shipments of a paediatric suspension goes live next Monday. Under the new flow, every urgent air shipment to South Africa needs a named approver in the regional team before it leaves the warehouse. You write to Marta, a colleague in another region, to ask her to nominate that approver and to confirm her team will use the new form. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Introduce the revised approval workflow for expedited shipments and say it starts next Monday.
Ask Marta to name one approver and one deputy in her region.
Request confirmation that her team will use the new form, with a reply date.

situation: Your active-ingredient supplier in Japan changed the particle-size specification for its latest lots, and you only found out from a line in a certificate of analysis. No change notice was sent. You write to Kenji Ahmed, your contact there, to ask for the change documentation and a short call, and to keep the next shipment on hold until you have spoken. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Explain that you noticed the new particle-size specification on the latest certificate of analysis.
State that no change notification reached you and ask for the supporting change documents.
Propose a call this week and say the next shipment stays on hold until then.

situation: You are updating your manager Julia about an oral solid dose tablet in Italy. For November and December the statistical forecast is about 35 percent lower than the commercial forecast, roughly 400,000 packs apart in total. You want her to know the gap, what you think explains it, and the meeting you will set up to agree one number. Keep it friendly and brief.
tasks: Tell Julia the statistical and commercial forecasts differ by about 35 percent for November and December.
Explain the likely reasons, such as a tender assumption sales has not shared with planning.
Say you will organise a consensus meeting next week and ask her to join if possible.

situation: A shipment of clinical-supply kits for a trial site in Japan arrived on time, but the certificate of analysis for one component is missing, so quality cannot release the lot. The trial starts dosing in nine days. You write to your supplier contact Sofia and ask for the certificate by Wednesday. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Tell Sofia the kits arrived on time but cannot be released without the component certificate.
Ask her to send the signed certificate of analysis by Wednesday midday.
Mention the dosing start in nine days and ask her to confirm a sending time.

situation: A market in Italy could run out of the 50 mg strength of a cold-chain biologic in about three weeks, while the next ocean shipment lands in six. Katarina Larsen, who leads allocation in another region, has not answered two earlier emails about releasing some stock. You need a decision from her. Be firm but polite.
tasks: State that Italy may run out of the 50 mg strength in about three weeks.
Remind Katarina that your two earlier emails about releasing stock are still unanswered.
Ask for a decision on the allocation by Thursday and offer a call to agree it.

situation: You want to build a safety-stock buffer of about two extra weeks for a respiratory product in Brazil, which will tie up roughly 600,000 dollars of working capital until March. Chloe, who works in the finance team of another region, must approve it. You are asking her approval, so explain why the risk justifies it and that the buffer is temporary. Be reassuring.
tasks: Explain that you propose two extra weeks of safety stock for Brazil because of variable lead times.
State the working capital involved and say the buffer will be released by March.
Ask Chloe for approval by Friday and offer to share the supporting numbers.

situation: Your system never warned you that stock of a vial-based injectable was getting low in Japan, because the reorder point still reflects demand from two years ago. Samir, who runs purchasing for a customer hospital group, uses more than you assumed. You write to him to ask for his actual monthly usage so you can reset the reorder point. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that your reorder point was based on old demand and raised no alert.
Ask Samir for his actual monthly usage over the last six months.
Say you will reset the reorder point and confirm the new level within a week.

situation: From January every planning report must follow a new naming convention, and you manage forty recurring files that other teams link to. Andre, a peer who owns the reporting standard, did not provide a mapping from old to new names. You are concerned that links will break. Write to him and ask for a mapping and a transition period. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Say you understand the new naming convention is mandatory from January.
Point out that about forty recurring reports are linked from other teams and could break.
Ask Andre for a mapping table and a short parallel period with both names.

situation: Your weekly one-to-one with your manager Ingrid, Mondays at 9:00, now collides with the new Brazil operations stand-up. You have missed it twice this month. You want to propose a different rhythm, for example every second week for forty-five minutes. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Explain that the Monday 9:00 slot now clashes with the Brazil operations stand-up.
Propose a new rhythm, such as forty-five minutes every second Wednesday.
Ask Ingrid to choose a slot and send a new invitation.

situation: A tender customer in India has asked for written assurance of supply of a prefilled pen for the next twelve months. You cannot sign such a commitment yourself. You write to your manager Katarina to ask for approval to issue a letter based on the current plan, and for a legal review first. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Describe the tender customer request for a twelve-month written assurance of supply.
Ask Katarina to approve a letter based on the current supply plan and its stated assumptions.
Request a legal review before sending and propose a deadline for the customer reply.

situation:
You chaired a call with Chloe's regional team about a Polish distributor who wants a formal explanation for a back-order on a vial-based injectable that was never announced. Your notes:
- Back-order began 3 March after a filling delay
- No notice sent: regional team assumed planning would do it
- Distributor short of about 12,000 vials
- New ship date 22 March, partial 5,000 on 15 March
- Chloe drafts the apology letter by Friday
- You send the root-cause summary by Monday
tasks: Summarise what happened with the unannounced back-order and the decision on who failed to notify.
List the actions with owners and dates, including the letter and the root-cause summary.
Ask Chloe to confirm the new ship dates and flag who owns future back-order notices.

situation: The qualification of a new sub-supplier for a diabetes product is slower than your contact Marta Novak promised, and the delivery of a key component now shifts by three weeks, from 10 June to 1 July. The change affects Singapore's launch plan. You must send a formal complaint asking for a recovery plan. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that the sub-supplier qualification is slower than agreed and delivery moves by three weeks.
Explain the effect on the Singapore launch plan and why the new date is a concern.
Request a written recovery plan by Friday and a weekly status update until delivery.

situation: Your manager Yuki Walsh cancelled the quarterly review of the Chile cold-chain biologic plan and replaced it with a written update. You have three decisions pending that need discussion, including a change to the safety-stock policy. Write to Yuki to say the written update is not enough and ask for a short call. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Acknowledge that the quarterly review was replaced by a written update.
Explain that three decisions, including the safety-stock policy change, need a live discussion.
Ask Yuki for a thirty-minute call this week and offer two time slots.

situation: A wholesaler in South Africa says its last three deliveries of a cardiovascular tablet arrived short and has threatened to switch suppliers. You have started an investigation with the warehouse. You write to Laura Tanaka, a colleague in the regional commercial team, to update her on what you know and what happens next. Keep the tone neutral.
tasks: Report that three consecutive deliveries to the wholesaler arrived short and say what you know so far.
Explain the investigation with the warehouse and when you expect the first findings.
Tell Laura what she should say to the wholesaler in the meantime.

situation: A team member, Mark, returns to demand planning in Germany after six months away, and the forecasting process changed in that time: the tablet portfolio now uses a new demand-review template and a different tool. You update your manager on how you will bring him up to speed in his first two weeks. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell your manager that Mark returns on Monday after six months away.
Outline what has changed, including the new demand-review template and the new tool.
Describe the plan for his first two weeks and ask whether your manager wants to meet him on day one.

situation: A distributor in Singapore asks for a formal explanation of a back-order on a diabetes product that was never announced. You are writing to Elena, their purchasing contact, to explain the cause, give the new delivery dates and say what you will change so that notices come earlier. Stay friendly but clear.
tasks: Apologise that the back-order was not announced and briefly explain the cause.
Give the new delivery dates, including any partial shipment.
Describe the change you will make so the distributor gets warnings earlier.

situation: A temperature-controlled truck booked by your logistics supplier for Monday was not available, so a pallet of vial-based injectables sat on the dock in Turkey for six hours before another vehicle arrived. Priya Nair manages the account. You must raise it formally and ask for a plan. Be disappointed but professional.
tasks: State that the temperature-controlled truck was not available on the agreed Monday and a pallet waited six hours.
Explain the quality risk and the paperwork the deviation created for you.
Ask Priya for a root cause and a backup-vehicle arrangement by the end of the week.

situation: A contractor, Oliver, will cover a colleague's maternity leave in the inhaler planning team in Sweden and needs a fast ramp-up plan. You are telling a peer who works next to you what the plan is and how they can help. Stay friendly.
tasks: Introduce Oliver and say he starts on 3 November to cover the maternity leave.
Describe the ramp-up plan, with system access in week one and live supply reviews in week two.
Ask your peer to be Oliver's buddy for the first week.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, during the audit prep we found that the cleaning verification record for Line 3 was incomplete, with one signature missing. We have to re-check the line, which takes two days, so the batch release moves from Tuesday to Thursday. Can you tell the customer and keep the shipment slot for Friday? Hannah Brandt" Hannah works in a site in another region. You reply to her. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Acknowledge the incomplete cleaning verification record and the two-day re-check on Line 3.
Accept the move from Tuesday to Thursday only if the Friday shipment slot stays safe.
Ask Hannah for written confirmation of the revised release date and the corrective action.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, the clinical team says seasonal demand for the kits in Chile seems to be starting about three weeks earlier than usual. Does our forecast reflect that? I need your view for the S&OP pre-read on Thursday. Julia" Reply to Julia, your manager, with what you know and what you will do. Stay friendly.
tasks: Answer Julia's question: say whether the current forecast reflects the earlier seasonal start.
Describe what you will check, such as order history and clinic feedback, before Thursday.
Offer an updated number for the S&OP pre-read and ask her which version she prefers.

situation:
You met your peer Peter Ruiz to plan how a colleague from medical affairs will move into supply planning for a cold-chain biologic in Brazil. Now you must send him a follow-up. Your notes:
- She starts Monday 10 November
- Weeks 1-2: system training, you as buddy
- Week 3: shadows weekly supply call
- Peter requests her access by Friday
- Review in 30 days with the manager
- Open point: who covers her old projects
tasks: Summarise the decisions about her move into supply planning and her first month.
List the actions with owners and dates, including Peter's access request and your buddy role.
Ask Peter to confirm the plan and flag who covers her previous projects.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Hi Alex, I just saw that your audit of our Mexico site is scheduled for Tuesday 12 November, the same day as our supplier workshop on the diabetes product forecast. Can you still attend the workshop? We could move it to Thursday afternoon, or send you the slides. Best, Samir" Reply to Samir, your supplier contact, and decide how to handle the overlap. Stay neutral.
tasks: Confirm that the urgent site visit on 12 November overlaps with the supplier workshop.
Choose between moving the workshop to Thursday afternoon or receiving the slides, and explain why.
Ask Samir to send the new invitation or the slides by Monday.

situation: About 45,000 dollars of the Q3 budget for inhaler logistics in India remained unused, and you expect costs to rise in Q4 because of two extra airfreight shipments. You are writing to Katarina Moreau, who controls the budget in another region, to ask for a transfer of the unused amount into Q4. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that part of the Q3 inhaler logistics budget in India remained unused.
Request the transfer of about 45,000 dollars into Q4 and explain the two additional airfreight shipments.
Ask Katarina for her decision by the end of the month.

situation:
You chaired a meeting with Ben Hall, who coordinates clinical studies in Egypt, because the demand review for the clinical-supply kits had to be brought forward by two days to meet a finance deadline. Your notes:
- Review moves from Thursday 20 to Tuesday 18
- Finance closes forecast on Wednesday 19
- Ben sends updated enrolment numbers by Monday noon
- Planning loads 3 months of demand by Monday evening
- Site 4 delay still unresolved
- Draft kit plan shared Tuesday 9:00
- Ben approves final numbers on Tuesday
tasks: Summarise the decision to bring the demand review forward and the reason behind it.
List each action with its owner and date, from Ben's enrolment numbers to the draft kit plan.
Ask Ben to confirm the new timetable and flag the unresolved Site 4 delay.

situation: A wholesaler in Egypt reports that three consecutive deliveries of a prefilled pen arrived short, by between 40 and 120 units. You need delivery notes and goods-received records to find where the loss happens. You write to Yuki, the wholesaler's receiving manager. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Refer to the wholesaler's report that three consecutive deliveries arrived short.
Ask Yuki for the delivery notes and goods-received records for those three shipments.
Promise a written finding within five working days of receiving the documents.

situation: An urgent site visit has landed on the same day as the stakeholder workshop you planned with Nadia, a customer contact in Japan, for the prefilled pen. You are updating her that the workshop moves from Wednesday 5 November to Friday 7 November and what she can expect. Stay friendly.
tasks: Apologise for moving the workshop from Wednesday 5 November to Friday 7 November.
Explain briefly that an urgent site visit caused the overlap.
Say you will send a new invitation and the agenda by Tuesday.

situation: A launch of a clinical-supply kit in Germany is at risk because sea freight would arrive after the planned start. Air freight would cost about 38,000 euros extra. You need approval from Laura, who owns the budget in another region, and you want to explain the update clearly. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Explain that sea freight would arrive after the planned launch date in Germany.
State the extra cost of about 38,000 euros for air freight and why it protects the launch.
Request Laura's written approval by Wednesday so the booking can be made.

situation: A respiratory product ran low in India because the reorder point was set on old demand and the system raised no alert. Your manager Mei owns the planning parameters and nobody reviews them regularly. You want her to commission a parameter review. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Describe the near stock-out and explain that the reorder point reflected old demand.
Point out that the system raised no alert and that parameters are never reviewed.
Ask Mei to set up a quarterly parameter review and name an owner.

situation: A new tool replaces spreadsheets for tracking purchase order confirmations in Australia. Hannah Ruiz, a peer, kept updating the old spreadsheet, so you were unable to see confirmations for eleven orders. You are disappointed. Write to her and ask her to use the tool from now on. Be disappointed but professional.
tasks: Mention that the new tool replaced the confirmation spreadsheet last week.
Explain that eleven confirmations were missing from it and how this affected your planning.
Ask Hannah to enter all new confirmations in the tool by the end of each day.

situation: The message below arrived this morning. "Dear Alex, I understand a supplier of the cold-chain biologic changed a raw-material specification without telling us. Could you prepare a short impact assessment by Friday, including which batches are affected and what the customers have received? Kind regards, Yuki Nair" Reply to Yuki, your manager in Sweden. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Confirm that the supplier changed the raw-material specification without notice.
Agree to deliver the impact assessment by Friday, covering affected batches and customer shipments.
Ask whether quality should lead the supplier discussion and offer a status update on Wednesday.

situation: A product family of oncology infusions is moving from your team to the regional team in the UK on 1 January. You are writing to Marta, who leads that team, to confirm what is transferring, the date and what documents she will receive. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: State that the oncology infusion family transfers to the UK regional team on 1 January.
List what you will hand over, such as open orders, forecast files and supplier contacts.
Propose a handover meeting before the end of November.

situation: You go on parental leave on 15 December and Yuki Lindqvist will cover your open purchase orders for a device sub-assembly in Spain. Your manager has not given the cover system access or a handover slot yet. Write to your manager and raise the problem. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Remind your manager that you start parental leave on 15 December and open purchase orders need a cover.
Point out that Yuki still lacks system access and no handover slot exists.
Ask for access to be granted and two hours of handover to be scheduled before 5 December.

situation: A new sub-supplier qualification for a vial-based injectable is slower than expected and pushes delivery in the UK back by three weeks. A peer, Ingrid Reyes, knows another qualified source. You write to ask whether she can introduce you and share what she knows. Stay friendly.
tasks: Explain that the sub-supplier qualification is delayed and delivery shifts by three weeks.
Ask Ingrid if the alternative qualified source could cover a bridging order.
Request a short call or an introduction by the end of the week.

situation: A standard template for demand-review notes has been introduced across regions. It has eleven sections and your meetings produce a page of notes, so your team now spends an hour per review on formatting. Write to your manager Andre Hall and ask for a shorter version. Be firm but polite.
tasks: Acknowledge the new standard template for demand-review notes.
Explain that eleven sections add about an hour of formatting per review.
Propose a shorter template and ask Andre to raise it with the owner.

situation: The owner of a weekly shipment report for the prefilled pen is leaving at the end of the month and you inherit it. Ben Fischer, a peer in Ireland, built part of the macros. You ask him for a one-hour walkthrough and the documentation. Stay friendly.
tasks: Tell Ben that you are taking over the weekly report when the owner leaves.
Ask for a one-hour walkthrough of the macros and data sources.
Offer two time slots next week and ask him to share any notes.

situation:
You attended a meeting with your manager Katarina Novak because a country in Egypt moved its launch of a cardiovascular tablet forward by six weeks. Your notes:
- New launch 12 January, not 23 February
- Initial stock 80,000 packs needed by 5 January
- Plan to use existing stock plus rush batch
- Production slot requested for 20 November
- You send revised forecast Friday
- Open point: artwork approval date
tasks: Summarise the decision to follow the new launch date and the stock needed.
List actions with owners and dates, including the production slot request and the revised forecast.
Ask Katarina to confirm and flag the open point on artwork approval.

situation: You will be on leave for two weeks from 17 November and your colleague Ingrid Ahmed will cover your oral solid dose tablet products in Australia. You write to ask her to take over, tell her what to watch and how to reach you in an emergency. Keep the tone formal.
tasks: Ask Ingrid to cover your tablet products in Australia from 17 November for two weeks.
Explain the main points to monitor, such as the weekly shipment and the open purchase orders.
Say when you will send the handover document and how to contact you in a real emergency.
